questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A rectangular parcel of undeveloped land contained three acres and had 150 feet of frontage on a public street. The applicable zoning ordinance required that a buildable lot contain at least two acres and have frontage of not less than 100 feet on a public street.
A brother and sister owned the land as tenants in common, the brother owning a one-third interest and the sister owning a two-thirds interest. Neither of them owned any other real property.
The sister brought an appropriate action to partition the land and proposed that a two-acre rectangular lot with 100 feet of frontage be set off to her and that a one-acre rectangular lot with 50 feet of frontage be set off to the brother. The brother's defense included a demand that the land be sold and its proceeds be divided one-third to the brother and two-thirds to the sister.
Who will prevail?

choices.A: The brother, because partition by sale is the preferred remedy, unless a fair price is not the likely result of a sale.
choices.B: The brother, because the zoning ordinance makes it impossible to divide the land fairly.
choices.C: The sister, because partition by sale is not appropriate if the subject property can be physically divided.
choices.D: The sister, because the ratio of the two lots that would result from her proposal conforms exactly to the ownership ratio.

questions.explanation:
Inequitable partition in kind

Tenancy in common
Sister's 2 acres = buildable
Brother's 1 acre ≠ buildable
100 ft
50 ft
150 ft

Tenancy in common is shared ownership of property where each co-tenant has a separate share of the property, but the right to possess and enjoy the entire property (ie, separate but undivided interests). A co-tenant may bring an action to partition (ie, divide) the property and, absent an agreement to the contrary, a court must grant that request. There are two types of partition:

  • In kind – physical division of the property into distinct lots that are proportionate to each co-tenant's ownership interest
  • By sale – forced sale of the property where the proceeds are divided in accordance with each co-tenant's ownership interest

Partition in kind is the preferred method of partition. But when physical division of the land is impossible, impracticable, or inequitable, a court will grant a partition by sale (Choices A & C).

Here, the brother and sister are tenants in common on three acres of undeveloped land with 150 feet of street frontage. The sister proposed a partition in kind where the brother would receive his one-third interest (one acre with 50 feet of frontage). But the ordinance makes it impossible to divide the land fairly since it would prohibit the brother from building on his lot. Therefore, the brother will prevail in his demand for a partition by sale.

(Choice D) Although the sister's proposal divides the land in conformity with the ownership ratio, a partition in kind would be inequitable since the brother would not be able to build on his lot. Therefore, the land will be partitioned by sale and the proceeds will be divided proportionately—ie, one-third to the brother and two-thirds to the sister.

📌 Educational Objective

In a tenancy in common, a co-tenant may bring an action for partition in kind or by sale. If a partition in kind (ie, physical division of the land) is impossible, impracticable, or inequitable, a court will grant a partition by sale.

📚 References
  • Restatement (First) of Property § 72 (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (right to partition).
questions.zh-question:
一块矩形的未开发土地占地三英亩，临公共街道的面宽为150英尺。

适用的区划法规要求，可建筑地块须至少占地两英亩，且临公共街道的面宽不少于100英尺。

一对兄妹以按份共有（tenants in common）的方式拥有该土地，兄拥有三分之一的权益，妹拥有三分之二的权益。两人均未拥有任何其他不动产。

妹妹提起了适当的诉讼以分割土地，并提议将一个占地两英亩、临街面宽100英尺的矩形地块分给她，将一个占地一英亩、临街面宽50英尺的矩形地块分给哥哥。哥哥的抗辩包括要求出售该土地，并将其收益按哥哥三分之一、妹妹三分之二的比例进行分配。

谁将胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 哥哥，因为出售分割是优先的救济方式，除非出售不可能获得公平的价格。
zh-choices.B: 哥哥，因为区划法规使得公平分割该土地变得不可能。
zh-choices.C: 妹妹，因为如果标的财产可以进行物理分割，则不适合进行出售分割。
zh-choices.D: 妹妹，因为她提议所产生的两个地块的比例与所有权比例完全一致。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Concurrent estates

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：共有产权（tenancy in common）分割时，什么时候不能硬做按份实物分割（partition in kind），而要改成出售分割（partition by sale）。

三秒认题路径：

共有关系 → 申请分割 → 看能否建地块 → 不公允就卖地 → 兄长赢

核心法律规则

在tenancy in common里，共有人可以要求分割；一般先看partition in kind，也就是把土地实际切成若干块。Partition in kind是优先方案，但如果这种切法会变得impossible、impracticable或inequitable，法院就改判partition by sale，把卖地款按份额分。

这题里，妹妹的方案虽然按比例切成2英亩和1英亩，但兄长那块只有50英尺临街，不满足用途上的可建性，所以这不是“公平切地”，而是把他切成一块不能正常使用的地。考试上这就叫：实物分割表面上对齐比例，实质上却让一方拿到废地，所以要走卖地。

核心判例： Restatement (First) of Property § 72 强调，分割实物若不公允，就应改为出售分割。

思维导图

起点：共有土地要分割，先问能不能“实物切地”
YES：每块地都能正常使用，且分完不偏不倚 → 才考虑 partition in kind
NO：一刀切下去会出现不能建、不能用、明显失衡 → 进入 partition by sale
卡死点：兄长那块只有 50 ft frontage，连 zoning 的 100 ft 门槛都过不了，inequitable。
结论：不是看“比例切得像不像”，而是看“切完后能不能正常做地块”；本题要卖地，按 1/3 与 2/3 分钱。
答案：兄长胜，因为法院不能接受把他分到一块无法建造的地。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：妹妹切出来的两块地正好按 1/3 和 2/3 对应，似乎已经“公平”了。

但考试真正问的是：切完以后是不是还能当正常地块用；如果兄长那块不能建，就不是公平实物分割。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的比例看起来对不对」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键点是 zoning ordinance 让兄长那块地不能建造，所以实物分割会变得不公允，法院应改判出售分割。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“默认偏好”当成绝对规则了，忽略了实物分割不公允时要转卖地。

❌ 法律适用 | 选项前提错位

✕ C: 只盯着“能不能物理切开”，没看到切完后会让兄长拿到不可建地块。

❌ 事实误判 | 比例等于公平

✕ D: 以为份额对齐就够了，漏掉了 buildable 才是真正的可用性门槛。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看分割结果是否还能形成可用地块；比例像不像第二位，能不能正常使用才第一位。

考场速记

记住一句话：partition in kind 优先，但只要切完会让一方拿到“不能正常用”的地，法院就改成partition by sale。

口诀：先看能不能切，不能公允就卖；别被“比例对齐”骗了。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A landlord leased a commercial building to a tenant for five years. Rent was payable on the first day of each month, and the landlord retained the right to terminate the lease if the tenant defaulted. The lease term ended 18 months ago. However, the tenant has stayed in possession of the building and has continued to pay the rent on time. The landlord has continued to accept the rent.
The fair rental value of the building is now substantially more than what the tenant has been paying, and the landlord recently found a third party who will pay the higher rent. When the tenant paid the rent two months ago, the landlord accepted the rent. At the end of the month, the landlord told the tenant in writing that she had to vacate at the end of the following month. The tenant, who is still in possession of the building, has informed the landlord that she does not want to move and is willing to pay the current fair rental value.
The landlord has asked his lawyer for advice regarding the right to possession.
Who should the lawyer say is entitled to possession?

choices.A: The landlord, because he gave proper notice to terminate the tenancy.
choices.B: The landlord, because he retained the right to reenter.
choices.C: The tenant, because she has stated that she is willing to pay the current fair rental value.
choices.D: The tenant, because the landlord has not shown good cause to terminate the tenancy.

questions.explanation:
Types of tenancies

(leases on land)

Type Creation Duration Termination
Term of years Agreement (ie, lease) Fixed period (eg, one month, three years) End of term (automatic)
Breach of certain covenants (eg, rent, habitability)
Periodic tenancy Agreement
Presumed when lease has no specified termination date
Operation of law (eg, holdover tenant) 		Periodically renews until terminated End of period (proper notice)
Breach of certain covenants
Tenancy at will Agreement
Implied when person allowed to possess premises without paying rent 		Indefinite period At any time (reasonable notice)
Tenancy at sufferance Implied when tenant keeps possession after lease expires (ie, holdover tenancy) Continues until terminated Landlord evicts
Tenant vacates
Landlord accepts rent (forms periodic tenancy)

A tenant has the right to possess the premises during the term of the lease. A tenant who remains in possession after the lease term expires is a holdover tenant (ie, tenant at sufferance). The landlord can then:

  • file a lawsuit to remove the tenant from the property (ie, an unlawful detainer action) or
  • accept rent and hold the tenant to a periodic tenancy—ie, a tenancy that automatically renews for successive periods of time depending on how rent was computed under the original lease (eg, monthly).

Either party (ie, landlord or tenant) can terminate a periodic tenancy at the end of a period by giving proper notice. Notice is proper if it is given before the final period starts—eg, to terminate a month-to-month periodic tenancy on June 30, notice must be given by May 31.

Here, the tenant remained in possession of the building after her five-year lease term expired (holdover tenant). Since rent was computed monthly under the original lease, the landlord held her to a month-to-month periodic tenancy by accepting rent. And since the landlord gave her notice to vacate at the end of the following month before the start of that final month, notice was proper. Therefore, the landlord is entitled to possession.

(Choice B) Unless the lease expressly states otherwise, a landlord does not retain a right of reentry—ie, a right to reenter and retake possession of the premises if the tenant breaches the lease. Here, the landlord only retained the right to terminate the lease if the tenant defaulted on rent—not the right to reenter.

(Choice C) Although the tenant was willing to pay the current fair rental value for the property, the landlord was not obligated to lease the property to her.

(Choice D) A periodic tenancy can generally be terminated without cause. However, some courts have held that landlords must show good cause to terminate a periodic tenancy of federally subsidized residential housing. But since the landlord's property was a commercial building, he does not need to show good cause to gain possession.

📌 Educational Objective

A holdover tenant—ie, one who remains in possession of the premises after his/her lease term expires—can be held to a periodic tenancy if the landlord accepts additional payments of rent. Either party can terminate the periodic tenancy at the end of a period if notice is given before that period starts.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Property: Landlord & Tenant § 1.5 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (periodic tenancy).
  • Restatement (Second) of Property: Landlord & Tenant § 14.4 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (holdover tenant).

该建筑的公平市场租金价值现在远高于租户一直支付的金额，并且房东最近找到了一个愿意支付更高租金的第三方。当租户在两个月前支付租金时，房东接受了租金。在那个月底，房东书面通知租户，她必须在下个月底搬离。目前仍在占有该建筑的租户已告知房东，她不想搬走，并愿意支付当前的公平市场租金价值。

房东就占有权问题向其律师咨询。

律师应告知谁有权占有该建筑？

zh-choices.A: 房东，因为他发出了终止租赁关系的适当通知。
zh-choices.B: 房东，因为他保留了收回权。
zh-choices.C: 租户，因为她已表示愿意支付当前的公平市场租金价值。
zh-choices.D: 租户，因为房东未能证明有正当理由来终止租赁关系。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Types of tenancies

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：期满滞留承租人（holdover tenant）被房东接受租金后，会转成定期租赁（periodic tenancy），而房东只要在正确时间给出通知，就能结束占有并拿回房屋。

三秒认题路径：

租期到期 → 继续占用 → 房东收租 → 月租转化 → 提前通知 → 房东赢

核心法律规则

租期结束后还继续住的人，是期满滞留承租人（holdover tenant），考场意思：先看他已经没有原始租约下的占有权了。房东如果继续收租，通常就把关系变成定期租赁（periodic tenancy），考场意思：租约不再按原来的五年跑，而是按原来算租的周期自动续。终止通知（notice to terminate）只要在新一期开始前给到，就能在期末把租赁结束掉。这里房东原来按月收租，所以新关系是月对月；他在月末前提前通知，正好有效。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Property: Landlord & Tenant 的 holdover 规则锁定：收租会把 holdover 变成 periodic tenancy，再按周期提前通知即可终止。

思维导图

第 0 步
五年term of years结束后，租客还在住
第 1 步
房东继续收月租 → 关系改成月对月 periodic tenancy
第 2 步
房东在当月结束前发书面通知，要求下月末搬走
第 3 步
新一期开始前已通知 → 终止有效 → 房东取得占有
题眼：不是“能不能涨租”，而是“现在谁有占有权”
先看租期到没到？
到了 → 继续住 = holdover
再看房东收没收租？
收了 → 变成 periodic tenancy
最后看通知给没给早？
在下一期开始前通知 → 可终止
结论房东能拿回占有，选 A

考点陷阱

你可能会想：租客愿意按现价付租，又一直按时交租，房东是不是就不能赶她走。

但考试真正问的是：房东有没有在正确时间结束periodic tenancy，不是房东想不想继续出租，也不是市场价高不高。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的占用看起来合不合理」。

“good cause” 这种想法只会骗你往住宅补贴房那边跑；这题是商业楼，普通月对月租赁本来就能无因终止，只要通知对时就行。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干显示房东已接受续租后租金，形成按月的periodic tenancy；又在下一期开始前提前书面通知，所以他有权收回占有。

❌ 概念混淆 | 重新进入误判

✕ B: 把right to reenter当成保留占有权，题干只写了终止权，不是重入权。

❌ 事实误判 | 现价愿付偷换

✕ C: 租客愿付fair rental value，不代表房东必须继续租给她。

❌ 法律适用 | 好因终止错套

✕ D: 把good cause规则套到商业房，题干根本不是补贴住宅。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认定是否holdover，再看房东是否收租把它变成periodic tenancy，最后只查通知是否踩在下一期开始前。

考场速记

记住一句：holdover + 收租 = periodic tenancy，periodic tenancy + 提前通知 = 可终止。这题不要被“想继续住”“想多付租”“房东想涨价”带偏，真正决定答案的只有通知时点。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A married couple purchased a residence. They took title to the property as tenants by the entirety. Subsequently, they separated, with the husband moving out and the wife remaining in the residence with their minor child. The husband has filed an action to partition the residence, which the wife opposes.
How should the court rule on the husband's partition action?

choices.A: For the husband, because the couple is no longer living together in the residence.
choices.B: For the husband, because the court can order the sale of the residence rather than its physical division.
choices.C: For the wife, because she is living in the residence with their minor child.
choices.D: For the wife, because the couple is married.

questions.explanation:
Cotenants' right to partition

Type of tenancy Voluntary partition (by agreement of all cotenants) Involuntary partition (by request of one cotenant)
Tenancy in common ✓ ✓
Joint tenancy ✓ ✓
Tenancy by the entirety ✓

A tenancy by the entirety (TBE) is a type of cotenancy that is available only to married couples. As a result, the TBE terminates upon divorce and becomes a tenancy in common. While tenants in common can unilaterally request a partition分割请求：共有人请求法院将共有财产分割或出售。 (which the court must grant), a TBE can only be partitioned if both spouses consent. That is because tenants by the entirety are viewed as a single marital unit.

Here, the married couple took title to the residence as tenants by the entirety. Although the couple separated and no longer live together in the residence, they are still married (Choice A). This means that the TBE remains intact, and the husband cannot partition the residence without the wife's consent. Therefore, the court should rule for the wife.

(Choice B) Although courts prefer a partition in kind (ie, physical division of property), a court may order a partition by sale if physically dividing the property is not feasible or fair. But here, the court should not partition the residence by either method because the couple is still married and the wife opposes the partition action.

(Choice C) In many states, after a divorce, a former spouse residing in the family residence with a minor child may have the right to remain there for a statutory period. This would be relevant in a divorce action, but not this partition action.

📌 Educational Objective

A tenancy by the entirety is only available to married couples and can only be partitioned if both spouses consent.

📚 References
  • 41 Am. Jur. 2d Husband and Wife § 32 (2020) (no right to partition tenancy by the entirety without consent).
questions.zh-question:
一对已婚夫妇购买了一处住宅。他们以 tenancy by the entirety（夫妻共有产权）的方式获得了该房产的所有权。随后，他们分居，丈夫搬出，妻子则与他们的未成年子女继续居住在该住宅中。丈夫提起了分割该住宅的诉讼，但妻子表示反对。

法院应如何就丈夫的分割诉讼作出裁决？

zh-choices.A: 支持丈夫，因为这对夫妇已不再共同居住在该住宅中。
zh-choices.B: 支持丈夫，因为法院可以下令出售该住宅，而非进行实物分割。
zh-choices.C: 支持妻子，因为她正与他们的未成年子女居住在该住宅中。
zh-choices.D: 支持妻子，因为这对夫妇仍处于婚姻关系中。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Concurrent estates

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：tenancy by the entirety（共有整体） 还在不在，所以丈夫能不能单方面申请分割。

三秒认题路径：

已婚 → 共有整体 → 仍婚姻存续 → 需双方同意 → 不能强制分割

核心法律规则

抓住这条规则就够了

共有整体（tenancy by the entirety） 只适用于已婚夫妻，所以只要婚姻还在，这种共有就还在。分割（partition） 对 tenancy in common（按份共有） 可以单方请求，但对 tenancy by the entirety（共有整体），考试上要点是：必须双方同意 才能分割。

所以这里丈夫虽然搬走了，但两人还没离婚，TBE 仍然完整存在，法院不能只听丈夫一方就把房子拆开或卖掉。

核心判例： 41 Am. Jur. 2d Husband and Wife § 32 的规则就是：tenancy by the entirety 没有配偶同意，不能被单方分割。

思维导图

先看：这套房是什么共有？
是tenancy by the entirety（共有整体）
再看夫妻有没有离婚？
本题只是分居，没有离婚
卡死点：仍是已婚夫妻 → 共有整体还在 → 单方不能 partition
结论丈夫请求被挡回去，选妻子

考点陷阱

你可能会想：夫妻都分居了，丈夫已经离家，应该可以要求法院把房子分掉。

但考试真正问的是：婚姻关系还在不在。 只要还没离婚，tenancy by the entirety（共有整体） 就还在，丈夫不能单方面分割。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干已明确是夫妻共同持有 tenancy by the entirety，而两人只是分居、并未离婚，所以丈夫没有单方 partition 的权利。

❌ 概念混淆 | 分居当离婚

✕ A: 把 no longer living together 误当成婚姻结束。

❌ 法律适用 | 以卖代分误判

✕ B: 看到法院能卖房就以为丈夫能单方启动分割。

❌ 事实误判 | 亲子居住偷换

✕ C: 把 minor child 当成本题分割权来源。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定共有类型，再问婚姻是否仍存续；只要还是 tenancy by the entirety，就先挡掉单方分割。

考场速记

记住一句：tenancy by the entirety（共有整体） 是“夫妻合体”的共有，没离婚就不能单方 partition。

考到中间上诉或例外时再补口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，分别记 Injunction（禁令）、Certification（认证）、Class action（集体诉讼） 等法定例外。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A landlord and tenant entered into a one-year lease to rent a one-bedroom apartment in a multi-family dwelling. The tenant was a sculptor who spent much of her time working on art projects that could cause a significant amount of noise. The windows and doors in the apartment were lacking proper sealing and soundproofing for sculpting, but the landlord and the sculptor agreed to leave the property as is. They also agreed that the sculptor could create art pieces in the apartment. After one month passed, numerous neighbors complained to the sculptor that her sculpting activities were loud and disruptive. The sculptor decided to soundproof the windows and doors in her apartment, and she deducted those expenses from her monthly rental payment. The landlord is now filing an action against the sculptor for the full rental amount.
Who will likely succeed?

choices.A: The landlord, because the sculptor cannot withhold a portion of the rent for repairs.
choices.B: The landlord, because the sculptor committed waste by improving the property.
choices.C: The sculptor, because she made necessary improvements to the property.
choices.D: The sculptor, because the landlord did not provide adequate soundproofing.

questions.explanation:
Types of waste

Original premises

Permissive waste

Voluntary waste

Ameliorative waste

Although tenants have a duty to avoid waste, a tenant may generally commit ameliorative waste by changing the physical condition of the leased property in a manner that increases its value. However, those changes must be reasonably necessary for the tenant to use the property in a reasonable manner—and the landlord and tenant must not have agreed otherwise.

Here, the sculptor may have improved the value of the leased apartment by soundproofing the windows and doors. And though those improvements may have been necessary for the sculptor to create art pieces in the apartment, the landlord and the sculptor had agreed to leave the property as is (Choice C). Therefore, the sculptor was not permitted to commit ameliorative waste, and the landlord will likely succeed against the sculptor for the full rental amount.

(Choices A & D) A tenant may repair a defect and offset the cost against the tenant's rent if the landlord violated the implied warranty of habitability. This warranty is implied in most residential leases and requires that the landlord maintain the property such that it is reasonably suited for residential use (i.e., does not substantially threaten the tenant's health or safety). But here, the lack of soundproofing did not threaten the sculptor's health or safety, so she was not entitled to add soundproofing and deduct the cost from the rent based on the implied warranty.

📌 Educational Objective

Ameliorative waste occurs when a tenant changes the physical condition of the leased property in a manner that increases its value. Such changes are permitted if they are reasonably necessary for the tenant to use the property in a reasonable manner—unless the landlord and tenant have agreed otherwise.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Property: Landlord and Tenant § 12.2 (Am. L. Inst. 1977) (discussing ameliorative waste).
questions.zh-question:
主题：不动产（Real Property）—不动产所有权（Ownership of Real Property）

一名房东和一名承租人签订了一份为期一年的租约，租赁一套多户住宅（multi-family dwelling）中的一居室公寓。该承租人是一名雕塑家，她花费大量时间进行可能产生较大噪音的艺术创作。该公寓的窗户和门缺乏适合雕塑工作的适当密封和隔音（soundproofing），但房东与雕塑家同意按现状（as is）保留该房产。他们还同意雕塑家可以在公寓内创作艺术品。一个月后，许多邻居向雕塑家抱怨她的雕塑活动噪音很大且扰乱他人。于是，雕塑家决定对她公寓的窗户和门进行隔音处理，并将该笔费用从每月租金中扣除。房东现起诉雕塑家，要求其支付全额租金。
谁更可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 房东，因为雕塑家不能扣留部分租金用于维修（repairs）。
zh-choices.B: 房东，因为雕塑家通过改善房产（improving the property）而构成了 waste。
zh-choices.C: 雕塑家，因为她对该房产作出了必要的改进（necessary improvements）。
zh-choices.D: 雕塑家，因为房东没有提供足够的隔音（soundproofing）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Landlord-tenant law

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：承租人擅自给租赁房屋做增值改造，是否构成 改善性浪费（ameliorative waste），能不能拿“修了更好用”为理由抵扣房租。

三秒认题路径：

承租人改房屋 → 房屋增值 → 事先约定不改 → 不能抵租 → 房东赢

核心法律规则

只看本题要用的规则

改善性浪费（ameliorative waste）的意思是：承租人把房屋物理状态改了，而且改动让房屋更值钱，通常可能被允许。

但前提有两个：改动对正常使用来说必须是合理必要的，而且房东和承租人没有另行约定不能这样改。约定保留原状（leave as is），考场意思：你就不能自己把房子升级后再反过来扣房租。

本题里，声学隔音让房子更适合雕塑创作，但双方已经同意保留原状，所以这次改造不受保护，属于不允许的浪费。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Property: Landlord and Tenant § 12.2——承租人即使在增值，也不能违背双方约定擅自改房屋。

思维导图

原始租约
一卧室公寓
→
房屋原状
门窗未隔音
→
承租人改造
自行加隔音
→
法律关卡
ameliorative waste
→
结论
不能扣房租
1. 这是不是“改善性浪费”？
先看：改动是否让房屋更值钱。这里是“是”。
2. 能不能靠“需要使用”挡住？
再看：是否只是合理使用所必需。这里虽然有帮助，但 双方已约定 leave as is，这一关直接卡死。
3. 结果是什么？
结论：承租人不能单方升级后抵扣租金，房东可要全额房租。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然隔音更方便她做雕塑，而且邻居投诉很多，那她是在做“必要维修”，所以能扣房租。

但考试真正问的是：她有没有权利在双方已经说好“保留原状”的前提下，自己升级房屋再抵租。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题里真正的分界线不是“有没有帮助”，而是“有没有授权”和“是不是维修对抗缺陷”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 soundproofing 让房屋更适合使用、也可能增值，但双方已约定 leave as is，所以构成未经允许的改善性浪费，房东可要全额房租。

❌ 概念混淆 | 维修抵租误判

✕ A: 把 repairs 当成当然可扣租，但本题不是修缺陷对抗房东违约。

❌ 法律适用 | 必要改造误判

✕ C: 看到 necessary improvements 就放行，忽略了双方已先约定不能改。

❌ 事实误判 | 隔音缺陷偷换

✕ D: 把“门窗不隔音”说成房东违法，但题干没说房屋不适合居住。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓租约有没有先行约定，再看改动是不是增值；一旦有 leave as is，就直接排掉抵租思路。

考场速记

记住一句：能改善，不等于能擅改；能增值，不等于能抵租。 看到承租人自己升级房屋，先问有没有 leave as is，有的话通常就是房东赢。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A woman convinced her younger friend to purchase undeveloped land with her. The friend contributed 30 percent of the purchase price, and the woman contributed 70 percent. They took title to the property based on the percentage of their contributions. Subsequently, the friend, purporting to own the property outright, obtained a loan and gave a mortgage on the property to the lender. When the friend defaulted on the loan, the bank initiated a foreclosure action on the property.
The jurisdiction follows the lien theory of mortgages.
To what interest, if any, would the purchaser of the property at the foreclosure sale be entitled?

choices.A: The entire property, because the friend, as a co-owner, is deemed to be the woman's agent.
choices.B: A 30 percent interest, because that is the friend's ownership interest in the property.
choices.C: A 30 percent interest, because the applicable jurisdiction follows the lien theory of mortgages.
choices.D: No interest, because a co-owner of property needs the consent of the other co-owners to mortgage it.

questions.explanation:
Consent between cotenants in common (common examples)
Consent required
  • Convey entire co-owned property
  • Obtain exclusive possession over part of property
  • Bind other cotenants' interests in contract with third party
No consent required
  • Sell, lease, or devise personal ownership interest
  • Possess entire co-owned property
  • Extract minerals from co-owned property (unless committing waste)

Tenancy in common is a type of concurrent estate (ie, cotenancy) where each cotenant has a possibly unequal ownership interest in the property, an equal right to possess the whole property, but no right of survivorship. A tenant in common is free to bind his/her individual interest in the property (eg, by mortgaging it) without the other cotenant(s)' consent. However, a tenant in common has no right to bind other cotenant(s)' interests in the property. Any attempt to do so will not affect the other cotenant(s)' interests.†

Here, the woman and the friend shared the property as tenants in common, as evidenced by their unequal interests in the property. Although the friend was free to bind her 30 percent interest in the property, she had no right to bind the woman's interest in the property. As a result, the friend's attempt to give the lender a mortgage on the entire property was ineffective as to the woman's interest. This means that the purchaser at the foreclosure sale would only be entitled to the friend's 30 percent interest in the property.

†This is true unless the other cotenant(s) authorize or later ratify the transaction (not seen here).

(Choice A) The mere existence of a cotenancy does not create an agency relationship between the cotenants, so the friend is not deemed to be the woman's agent simply because the friend co-owns the property.

(Choice C) The friend was free to mortgage her 30 percent interest in the property regardless of which mortgage theory the jurisdiction follows.

(Choice D) In a tenancy by the entirety, neither spouse can mortgage the property without the other spouse's consent. But here, the woman and her friend were not spouses who shared the property as tenants by the entirety. Instead, they shared the property as tenants in common, and each was free to mortgage her interest in the property without the other's consent.

📌 Educational Objective

A tenant in common can bind his/her own interest in the co-owned property without the other cotenants(s)' consent but has no right to bind the other cotenant(s)' interests in the property.

📚 References
  • 20 Am. Jur. 2d Cotenancy and Joint Ownership § 93 (2020) (ability to bind other cotenants).
questions.zh-question:
一名女子说服了她年轻的朋友与她一起购买一块未开发的土地。该朋友支付了30%的购买价款，而该女子支付了70%。她们根据各自的出资比例取得了该财产的所有权。随后，该朋友声称自己完全拥有该财产，获得了一笔贷款，并以该财产向贷款人设定了抵押。当该朋友贷款违约时，银行对该财产提起了止赎诉讼。

该司法管辖区遵循抵押权的留置权理论 (lien theory of mortgages)。

在止赎拍卖中，该财产的购买人有权获得何种权益（如有）？

zh-choices.A: 整个财产，因为该朋友作为共同所有人，被视为该女子的代理人。
zh-choices.B: 30%的权益，因为那是该朋友在该财产中的所有权份额。
zh-choices.C: 30%的权益，因为所适用的司法管辖区遵循抵押权的留置权理论 (lien theory of mortgages)。
zh-choices.D: 无任何权益，因为财产的共同所有人需要获得其他共有人的同意才能抵押该财产。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Concurrent estates

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：共有租赁（tenancy in common）里，某个共有人只能处分自己的份额，不能替别人把整块地一起抵押出去。

三秒认题路径：

不等份额 → 共有租赁 → 只管自己份额 → 不能绑别人 → 拍卖只得 30%

核心法律规则

在共有租赁（tenancy in common）中，每个共有人对自己的份额有独立处分权，所以可以单独签抵押（mortgage），考场意思：只会把自己那一份押出去。

但一个共有人没有权利去绑住其他共有人的份额，考场意思：你不能因为她“自称全权所有”就把整块地都算进担保范围。

本题里朋友只拿了 30%，所以银行止赎后，买受人最多取得朋友的 30% 份额。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用；本题不问上诉，而是问共有人的处分范围。真正锁定结论的是共有租赁规则：只能处分自己的份额，不能单方影响他人份额。

思维导图

女方
70% 份额
+
朋友
30% 份额
→
共同持有土地
共有租赁
朋友把整块地拿去抵押，买受人能拿到多少？
先看：是不是共有租赁（tenancy in common）？
是：各自份额独立，能押自己的 30%
再看：她有没有权利替女方那 70% 也设担保？
没有：不能绑别的共有人的份额
结论：止赎买受人只继受朋友的 30% 份额。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她都“像是在代表整块地”去借钱了，银行是不是就能直接拿走整块地。

但考试真正问的是：她有没有权利把别人的份额一起抵押出去；答案是没有。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这一题对应的不是“谁看起来像真正老板”，而是“谁实际能处分哪一份”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干已经写明朋友只按出资比例持有 30%，所以她的抵押只能及于自己的份额，拍卖买受人也只能拿到这 30%。

❌ 概念混淆 | 代理关系误判

✕ A: 把共有人硬说成agent，题干根本没给代理授权。

❌ 法律适用 | 产权理论误判

✕ C: lien theory 只管抵押理论，不改她只能押自己份额的规则。

❌ 事实误判 | 共有类型偷换

✕ D: 把本题偷换成夫妻共有，题干明明是普通共有人。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定共有类型，再问“她能绑谁的份额”，别被“整块地被抵押”的表面动作带跑。

考场速记

记住一句：共有租赁（tenancy in common）里，能动的只有自己的份额，不能顺手把别人的也押掉。

速记口诀：先看“谁有份额”，再看“谁能处分”；没有授权，就只能各管各的。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A man died, leaving a will that devised his land to "my wife for life, remainder to my son and the heirs of his body. But if my son dies without children, then the land shall go to my nephew." Subsequently the wife died, devising all of her estate to the son. The son then sold the land to a neighbor. The son died shortly thereafter, survived only by a daughter. The daughter has now brought an appropriate action to quiet title against the neighbor and the nephew.
The common law Rule Against Perpetuities is unmodified in the jurisdiction. The fee tail, which has been abolished by statute, is interpreted as a fee simple absolute.
In this action, who will likely prevail?

choices.A: The daughter, because the son's conveyance to the neighbor extinguished the nephew's interest.
choices.B: The neighbor, because the son held the land in fee simple absolute.
choices.C: The nephew, because he held the remainder following the son's interest.
choices.D: The nephew, because the language in the man's will did not create an interest in the son.

questions.explanation:
Man
→
to my wife for life
Life estate
→
remainder to my son and the heirs of his body
Vested remainder in fee tail
but if my son dies without children, then to my nephew
Contingent remainder
→
Neighbor
Fee simple absolute
Fee simple absolute to son (no entail to daughter or remainder to nephew)

There are three types of freehold estates:

  • Fee simple – lasts for an indefinite and potentially infinite duration (e.g., "to A and his heirs")
  • Fee tail – lasts until the original grantee's lineage dies out (e.g., "to A and the heirs of his body")
  • Life estate – terminates upon the death of an individual serving as the governing life (e.g., "to A for life")

Fee tails were historically used to keep land in a lineage but have been abolished by statute in almost every jurisdiction. Modern law interprets the fee tail as giving the first grantee a fee simple absolute.

Here, the man devised his son a fee tail that became possessory upon the mother's death (Choice D). Because this jurisdiction likely interprets a fee tail as a fee simple absolute, neither the daughter nor the nephew held a future interest (Choices A and C). When the son sold to the neighbor, the neighbor acquired a fee simple absolute and will likely prevail .

*In jurisdictions that still recognize fee tails, a holder may "disentail" the estate by conveying a fee simple absolute to a third party.

📌 Educational Objective

Nearly every jurisdiction has abolished the fee tail, and a conveyance of this estate is commonly interpreted as giving the first grantee a fee simple absolute.
questions.zh-question:
一名男子去世，其遗嘱中将他的土地遗赠给“我的妻子终身保有，剩余权益归于我的儿子及其直系后嗣。但如果我的儿子死时无子女，则土地应归我的侄子所有。”后来，妻子去世，将其所有遗产遗赠给儿子。之后，儿子将该土地卖给了一位邻居。不久后，儿子去世，仅留下一名女儿。女儿现在对邻居和侄子提起了适当的确权诉讼 (action to quiet title)。

在该司法管辖区，普通法中的“反永久所有权规则 (Rule Against Perpetuities)”未经修改，而限定继承地产 (fee tail) 已被法规废除。

在此诉讼中，谁可能会胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 女儿，因为她是儿子身体的继承人。
zh-choices.B: 邻居，因为能够触发侄子权益的条件没有发生。
zh-choices.C: 侄子，因为儿子死时没有男性继承人。
zh-choices.D: 邻居，因为儿子以完全拥有绝对所有权 (fee simple absolute) 的形式持有该土地。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Present estates

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：遗嘱里写出类似 fee tail（fee tail） 的语言后，因该州已用法规废除 fee tail，法院会不会把它直接当成 fee simple absolute（完全所有权） 给第一个受赠人。

三秒认题路径：

看见 heirs of his body → 想 fee tail → 看州法已废除 → 变成 fee simple absolute → 邻居赢

核心法律规则

先抓规则，再看这题怎么落

fee simple absolute（完全所有权）：期限最长、没有未来利益卡住，持有人现在卖掉就能把完整权利转出去。
life estate（终身地产）：只跟着某个人活着，死了就结束。
fee tail（限嗣继承地产）：传统上跟“heirs of his body”绑定，但本题州里已用法规废除，所以通常直接解释成给第一受赠人一个 fee simple absolute（完全所有权）。

核心判例： 本题不靠特定判例推翻结论，关键是“fee tail 已被废除后，通常按 fee simple absolute 处理”这一现代规则。

思维导图

先看遗嘱语言：to my wife for life → remainder to my son and the heirs of his body
关卡1：这是不是 fee tail？是。
废除 fee tail 的州法：直接把它当成 fee simple absolute 给儿子
关卡2：那孙女和侄子有没有未来利益？没有。儿子拿到的是完整所有权，能卖给邻居。
终点：邻居拿到儿子的完整权利，静默题眼就是“儿子卖出时自己已经有完整所有权”
错觉提醒：别被 “if my son dies without children” 骗去想侄子一定有权利；在废除 fee tail 的州，这句通常不再给他可执行的未来利益

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然写了“如果儿子没孩子就给侄子”，那侄子应该有未来利益，女儿也可能继承。
但考试真正问的是：这句话在 fee tail（限嗣继承地产） 被废除的州里，还能不能真的卡住儿子的权利。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。（这题对应的就是：州法已经把 fee tail 改写了，题干里那句限制不再拦住儿子的完整处分权。）

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的 heirs of his body 在本州已被当成 fee simple absolute（完全所有权），所以儿子卖给邻居时能转出完整权利。

❌ 事实误判 | 销售灭绝误判

✕ A: 误以为儿子一卖，侄子的权利就被“消灭”了。

❌ 法律适用 | 余留利益误判

✕ C: 把 remainder 当成侄子已拿到稳定未来利益。

❌ 概念混淆 | 赠与对象误判

✕ D: 误把“heirs of his body”读成儿子根本没拿到权利。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认出 fee tail，再马上查州法是否废除；一旦废除，默认直接给第一受赠人 fee simple absolute。

考场速记

记住一句：heirs of his body 先想到 fee tail，再想到“多数州已废除，通常改读成 fee simple absolute”，所以先受赠人往往赢。
这题的 shortcut 就是：看到 fee tail 先查废除规则，没别的特别限制时，直接默认第一人拿完整所有权。

question_analysis.skill_tested: apply statutory fee tail abolition

reason.en: Creates a possessory life estate that must terminate before the son's interest becomes possessory.
reason.zh: 创设占有性终身地产，须在其终止后儿子方可取得占有权。

keywords.text: remainder to my son and the heirs of his body

reason.en: Classic fee tail phrasing that controls how future interests are classified.
reason.zh: 典型限嗣继承用语，决定未来权益如何归类。

keywords.text: if my son dies without children

reason.en: Triggers the nephew's alternative devise only if the son dies childless.
reason.zh: 仅在儿子无子女去世时触发侄子替代取得条款。

reason.en: Signals that common law fee tail rules do not govern the son's interest.
reason.zh: 表明普通法限嗣继承规则不再支配儿子权益。

reason.en: Defines the estate the son actually holds after statutory conversion.
reason.zh: 界定法定转化后儿子实际持有的地产类型。

keywords.text: sold the land to a neighbor

reason.en: A fee simple owner can pass full title, defeating later claims by daughter or nephew.
reason.zh: 绝对继承地产权人可转让完整产权，排除女儿或侄子后续主张。

reason.en: Frames the dispute as determining who presently owns the land.
reason.zh: 将争议定性为判定土地现时归属何人。

A.text: son's conveyance to the neighbor extinguished the nephew's interest

reason.en: Misapplies fee tail disentailing logic instead of recognizing the son already held fee simple absolute.
reason.zh: 误用限嗣继承解除逻辑，而未认识到儿子已持有绝对无条件继承地产。

B.text: son held the land in fee simple absolute

label.zh: 儿子经转化后的地产类型

reason.en: States the controlling rule that makes the neighbor the present owner.
reason.zh: 陈述决定邻居为现时所有权人的关键规则。

reason.en: Assumes a surviving future interest in the nephew despite statutory abolition of the fee tail.
reason.zh: 在限嗣继承已被法定废止的情况下仍假设侄子享有未来权益。

D.text: did not create an interest in the son

label.zh: 否认儿子取得遗赠权益

reason.en: Incorrectly treats the son as having no interest when he received a possessory converted estate.
reason.zh: 错误认为儿子未取得权益，实则其已取得经转化的占有性地产。

highlights.text: remainder to my son and the heirs of his body

reason.en: The heirs-of-the-body wording normally creates a fee tail, which is the starting point for classification.
reason.zh: “身体继承人”措辞通常创设限嗣继承，是权益分类分析的起点。

highlights.text: The fee tail, which has been abolished by statute, is interpreted as a fee simple absolute.

label.zh: 法定限嗣继承转化规则

reason.en: This sentence resolves the case by converting the son's interest into alienable fee simple absolute.
reason.zh: 该句通过将儿子权益转化为可转让的绝对无条件继承地产而决定案件结果。

highlights.text: The son then sold the land to a neighbor.

reason.en: Because the son held fee simple absolute, this sale passed full title to the neighbor.
reason.zh: 因儿子持有绝对无条件继承地产，此次转让使邻居取得完整产权。

highlights.text: survived only by a daughter

label.zh: 儿子去世留有一名后裔

reason.en: May mislead examinees to apply traditional fee tail succession to the daughter.
reason.zh: 可能误导考生适用传统限嗣继承由女儿继承的规则。

highlights.text: if my son dies without children, then the land shall go to my nephew

reason.en: Creates a contingent remainder in common law analysis, but is defeated once the son holds and conveys fee simple absolute.
reason.zh: 在普通法分析下创设或有式余产，但儿子取得并转让绝对无条件继承地产后即失效。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
Sixty years ago by a properly executed and recorded deed, a man conveyed a tract of land: "To my grandson for life, then to my grandson's widow for her life, then to my grandson's child or children in equal shares." At that time, the grandson was six years old.
Shortly thereafter, the man died testate. The grandson was the man's only heir at law. The man's will left his entire estate to his church.
Twenty-five years ago, when he was 41, the grandson married a woman who was then 20 years old; they had one child, a son. The grandson's wife and son were killed in an automobile accident three years ago when the son was 21. The son died testate, leaving his entire estate to a charity. His father, the grandson, was his sole heir at law.
Two years ago, the grandson married another woman. They had no children. This year, the grandson died testate, survived by his widow, to whom he left his entire estate.
The common law Rule Against Perpetuities is unchanged by statute in the jurisdiction.
In an appropriate action to determine ownership of the land, the court should find that title is vested in whom?

choices.A: The charity, because the son had a vested remainder interest (as the only child of the grandson) that it inherited, the life estate to the grandson's widow being of no force and effect.
choices.B: The church, because the grandson's widow was unborn at the time of conveyance and, hence, the remainder violated the Rule Against Perpetuities.
choices.C: The grandson's widow, because her life estate and her inheritance from the grandson (who was the man's sole heir at law and who was the son's sole heir at law) merged the entire title in her.
choices.D: The grandson's widow for life under the terms of the man's deed, with the remainder to the charity as the successor in interest to the son, the grandson's only child.

questions.explanation:
Man conveys land
Son dies & devises estate to charity
Grandson dies
Grandson
Life estate
Widow
Remainder in life estate
Life estate
Son / Charity
Son's remainder in FSA
Charity's remainder in FSA
Present estate
Future interest
FSA = Fee simple absolute.

A life estate is a present possessory interest in land that terminates on the death of an individual. The future-interest holder becomes entitled to possession once that death occurs. The future interest is either a reversion (if retained by the grantor) or a remainder (if created in someone other than the grantor). Both are fully transferable inter vivos,† devisable by will, and descendible by inheritance.

Here, the man conveyed a life estate to his grandson, which would pass first to the grandson's widow for life (remainder in life estate) and then to the grandson's child or children (remainder in fee simple absolute). The grandson had just one child, a son. Since the son died testate (ie, with a will), he effectively left his remainder interest in the land to the charity. Therefore, after the grandson's death, the widow had a life estate and the charity had the son's remainder interest (Choices A & C).

†At common law and in a minority of jurisdictions, contingent remainders cannot be transferred inter vivos.

(Choice B) The Rule Against Perpetuities (RAP) renders a future interest void if there is any possibility that it could vest more than 21 years after the death of some relevant person alive when the interest was created. But here, the widow's remainder interest did not violate RAP because it necessarily vested at the death of the grandson.

📌 Educational Objective

The future interest that follows a life estate is either a reversion (if held by the grantor) or a remainder (if created in someone other than the grantor). Both are transferable, devisable, and descendible.

📚 References
  • Restatement of Property § 157 (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (discussing the classification of remainders).
questions.zh-question:
六十年前，一名男子通过一份经合法签署并登记的契据，转让了一块土地：“终身授予我的孙子，然后终身授予我孙子的遗孀，然后平均分配给我孙子的一个或多个子女。” 当时，孙子六岁。

此后不久，该男子留有遗嘱去世。孙子是该男子唯一的法定继承人。该男子的遗嘱将其全部遗产留给了他的教会。

二十五年前，孙子41岁时，娶了一位当时20岁的女子；他们育有一子。三年前，孙子的妻子和儿子在一场车祸中丧生，当时儿子21岁。儿子留有遗嘱去世，将其全部遗产赠予一家慈善机构。他的父亲，即孙子，是其唯一的法定继承人。

两年前，孙子再婚。他们没有孩子。今年，孙子留有遗嘱去世，其遗孀尚在，他将全部遗产留给了她。

在该司法管辖区内，普通法上的 Rule Against Perpetuities（反永久所有权规则）未被成文法所改变。

在一项旨在确定该土地所有权的适当诉讼中，法院应认定所有权归属于谁？

zh-choices.A: 该慈善机构，因为儿子（作为孙子的唯一子女）拥有一项既得剩余权益，该慈善机构继承了此权益，而授予孙子遗孀的终身地产权是无效的。
zh-choices.B: 该教会，因为孙子的遗孀在转让时还未出生，因此，该剩余权益违反了 Rule Against Perpetuities。
zh-choices.C: 孙子的遗孀，因为她的终身地产权以及她从孙子处（孙子是男子的唯一法定继承人，也是儿子的唯一法定继承人）继承的财产，使全部所有权并入其名下。
zh-choices.D: 孙子的遗孀根据男子契据的条款拥有终身权益，剩余权益则归于慈善机构，作为孙子唯一子女（儿子）的权益继承人。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Future interests

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：生前受让的未来利益，在先后死亡与遗嘱转让后，最后到底是孙子的配偶的终身地产（life estate），还是慈善机构继受的余留权益（remainder）。

三秒认题路径：

先看赠与结构 → 再看谁活到谁死 → 再看利益能否遗嘱转让 → 最后锁定当前权利人

核心法律规则

终身地产（life estate）后面接的未来利益，若由授予人之外的人创设，就是余留权益（remainder）；考场意思：它不是“等不到就作废”的那种普通猜测，而是可以直接跟着生命事件往下走。

既得余留权益（vested remainder）和或有余留权益（contingent remainder）在通常法下都可转让、遗嘱处分、继承；考场意思：持有人死了，利益不会自动回到原授予人手里。

本题里，孙子的唯一子女是儿子；儿子死后把自己在土地中的未来利益留给了慈善机构，所以等孙子死时，先轮到孙子的现任遗孀（widow）拿终身地产，之后由慈善机构接手余留权益。

核心判例： Restatement of Property § 157 - 说明余留权益的分类与可转让性，锁定本题不会因为“继受人已出生或已死亡”而自动消灭。

思维导图

1. 先看赠与条款：“给孙子终身，之后给孙子的遗孀终身，再给孙子的子女平分”
结论这是典型的终身地产 + 余留权益链条，不是回到授予人的复归权。
2. 再看关键人物变化：孙子有一个儿子，儿子后来又把自己的未来利益写进遗嘱给了慈善机构
规则余留权益可以遗嘱处分（devise），所以儿子死后，慈善机构成为继受人。
3. 最后问：RAP 会不会把这份余留权益打掉？
否决点 不会，因为遗孀的权益在孙子死亡时必然到来，不存在“超过 21 年后才可能才得 vest”的风险。
终点
答案孙子的遗孀先拿终身地产，慈善机构拿后续余留权益。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：孙子的儿子死了，权益是不是就“没了”，或者遗孀是后来才出现，所以整段赠与被 RAP 搞坏了。

但考试真正问的是：司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这里对应的是未来利益是否能继续传下去，不是故事里谁先死谁后死的戏剧性。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干给的是“给孙子的遗孀终身，再给子女”，所以孙子死后先由遗孀拿终身地产，儿子生前已取得的余留权益则由慈善机构承接。

❌ 概念混淆 | 既得权误判

✕ A: 把儿子当成唯一终局权利人，忽略了遗孀的先行终身地产。

❌ 法律适用 | RAP套错题

✕ B: 看到 Rule Against Perpetuities 就乱套，但这里的权益在孙子死时必然到来。

❌ 事实误判 | 合并权利偷换

✕ C: 把遗孀后来的继承和终身地产硬合并成完整所有权，题干没有给这个结果。

这题建议用什么方法？

先拆赠与顺序，再查未来利益是否可遗嘱处分，最后只问是否有人先把权益截走。

考场速记

记住一句：“终身地产后面的余留权益，通常可转让、可遗嘱处分、可继承。” 本题看到遗孀先拿、子女再接，就先别被 RAP 吓跑，先顺着“人死了，利益还在不在”去找答案。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A landlord leased an apartment to a tenant on a month-to-month basis beginning on the first of the month, with rent payable monthly. Five months into the lease, the tenant failed to pay rent. The landlord then sued the tenant for possession for nonpayment of rent. The tenant successfully defended this suit on the ground that the apartment was uninhabitable and that, accordingly, no rent was properly payable.
On May 7, immediately following the court order in the tenant's favor, the landlord served the tenant with a written but not notarized notice to terminate the tenancy and to vacate the apartment on or before June 30.
On July 1, the tenant was still in possession, nothing had changed, and the landlord brought an appropriate action for possession. The tenant prevailed.
What is the most likely reason for the court's decision?

choices.A: A six-month notice was required to terminate this periodic tenancy.
choices.B: The landlord did not give the tenant a notarized notice of termination.
choices.C: The landlord's notice to terminate was improper, because it was given to the tenant more than one month before the required termination date.
choices.D: The landlord was attempting to terminate the tenancy as a reaction to the tenant's defense in the previous lawsuit.

questions.explanation:
Prohibited landlord conduct
Retaliation Increasing rent or terminating lease because tenant exercised legal right—eg:
  • reporting housing code violation
  • organizing tenants' association
Discrimination
(Fair Housing
Act)		 Refusing to rent or negotiate lease based on tenant's race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, gender, familial status, or disability

A periodic tenancy automatically continues for successive periods of time (eg, month to month) until either the landlord or tenant gives notice to terminate the tenancy. However, most jurisdictions prohibit a landlord from terminating a residential lease when:

  • the landlord is in the business of renting residential property
  • the tenant has complied with his/her lease obligations and
  • the landlord is retaliating against the tenant (eg, increasing rent, terminating a lease) for exercising a legal right in good faith and with reasonable cause.

Here, the landlord leased an apartment to the tenant (business of renting residential property) and later sued the tenant for unpaid rent. The tenant successfully defended that suit by challenging the apartment's habitability (exercise of a legal right). As a result, no rent was owed (compliance with lease obligations). The landlord then attempted to terminate the tenant's lease (retaliation). Therefore, the tenant likely prevailed in the landlord's action for possession because the termination was a retaliatory reaction to the tenant's defense in the previous lawsuit.

(Choice A) Six months' notice is required to terminate a year-to-year periodic tenancy. But a periodic tenancy with successive periods of less than one year (as seen here) can be terminated at the end of a period if notice is given before the period starts—eg, terminating a month-to-month periodic tenancy on June 30 requires notice by May 31.

(Choice B) Notice to terminate a periodic tenancy generally must be in writing but does not need to be notarized.

(Choice C) A month-to-month periodic tenancy can be terminated at the end of a month through notice given any time before the start of that month. Therefore, notice given on May 7 to vacate the premises by June 30 would have been proper had the termination not been retaliatory.

📌 Educational Objective

Most jurisdictions prohibit a landlord from terminating a residential lease when (1) the landlord is in the business of renting residential property, (2) the tenant has complied with his/her lease obligations, and (3) the landlord is retaliating against the tenant for exercising a legal right in good faith and with reasonable cause.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Prop.: Landlord & Tenant §§ 14.8–14.9 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (listing remedies for retaliatory action by landlord).
questions.zh-question:
房东将一套公寓按月租给租户，租期从每月的第一天开始，租金按月支付。租约开始五个月后，租户未能支付租金。房东随后因租户未付租金而起诉要求收回公寓。租户以公寓不适合居住，因此无需支付租金为由，成功地为自己辩护。

5月7日，在法院作出有利于租户的判决后，房东立即向租户送达了一份书面但未经公证的通知，要求其终止租赁关系，并于6月30日或之前搬离公寓。

到了7月1日，租户仍在公寓内，情况没有任何变化，房东提起了适当的占有之诉。租户胜诉。

法院作出此判决最可能的原因是什么？

zh-choices.A: 终止此定期租赁需要提前六个月通知。
zh-choices.B: 房东没有向租户发出经公证的终止通知。
zh-choices.C: 房东的终止通知不当，因为其在要求的终止日期前一个多月就已向租户发出。
zh-choices.D: 房东试图终止租赁是对租户在先前诉讼中进行辩护的一种反应。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Duties Of Landlord

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：房东能不能因为租客先前主张居住性抗辩，就把月租性租约报复性终止。

三秒认题路径：

月租租约 → 先前胜诉 → 终止通知 → 是否报复 → 不能终止

核心法律规则

月对月的 周期性租赁（periodic tenancy） 会按期自动续下去，直到一方按规则通知终止。书面通知（written notice） 通常够了，考试里不是 公证（notarized） 才有效。

但多数法域禁止房东在住宅出租业务中，因租客善意行使合法权利后，出于 报复（retaliation） 去涨租或终止租约。考场意思：租客先前打赢 居住性抗辩（habitability defense），后面房东再赶人，法院会先看是不是报复。

核心判例： 本题对应的关键逻辑就是 retaliatory eviction 规则：房东不能因为租客依法抗辩成功，就反手终止住宅租约。

思维导图

先问：房东这次终止，表面上像不像只是正常月租终止？
①房东在经营住宅出租业务，租客也是按月续租。
②租客先前用 habitability defense 成功挡掉欠租诉讼，说明他在行使合法权利。
③ 房东随后发出终止通知，时间上紧跟着租客胜诉。
卡死点：终止原因是 retaliation，不是单纯的租期结束。
结论：即使通知形式基本像样，只要是报复性终止，租客还是能赢。
答案落点：法院保护的是租客行使权利，不让房东用赶人来惩罚他。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：房东的通知是不是输在 notarized、或者输在通知日期算错了。

但考试真正问的是：房东是不是在租客赢了居住性抗辩后，拿终止租约来报复他。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的关键点是：租客先用 居住性抗辩 打赢欠租案后，房东立刻发出终止通知，这正是报复性终止的典型信号。

❌ 事实误判 | 租期类型看错

✕ A: 把月租租约当成年租，six-month 规则用错对象了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 公证要求误判

✕ B: 以为终止通知必须公证，命题人就想骗你把形式要求想得太重。

❌ 法律适用 | 提前通知误判

✕ C: 这里不是通知太早，而是通知本身带着报复动机。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“报复终止”这个禁区，再把通知形式和期限当成次要背景扫一眼。

考场速记

记住：月租租约可以正常通知终止，但 retaliatory eviction 不行；只要是因为租客善意行使合法权利，房东就容易输。

口诀：先看是不是 retaliation，再看通知形式。能救济不代表能报复。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
An elderly man leased a barn to his neighbor for a term of three years. The neighbor took possession of the barn and used it for his farming purposes. The lease made the elderly man responsible for structural repairs to the barn, unless they were made necessary by actions of the neighbor.
One year later, the elderly man conveyed the barn and its associated land to his granddaughter "subject to the lease to my neighbor." The neighbor paid the next month's rent to the granddaughter. The next day a portion of an exterior wall of the barn collapsed because of rot in the interior structure of the wall. The wall had appeared to be sound, but a competent engineer, on inspection, would have discovered its condition. Neither the granddaughter nor the neighbor had the barn inspected by an engineer. The neighbor was injured as a result of the collapse of the wall.
The elderly man had known that the wall was dangerously weakened by rot and needed immediate repairs when the neighbor took possession but had not told the neighbor or his granddaughter. There is no applicable statute.
The neighbor brought an appropriate action against the elderly man to recover damages for the injuries he sustained. The granddaughter was not a party.
Which of the following is the most appropriate comment concerning the outcome of this action?

choices.A: The neighbor should lose, because he failed to inspect the barn.
choices.B: The neighbor should lose, because the granddaughter assumed all of the elderly man's obligations by reason of the neighbor's attornment to her.
choices.C: The neighbor should recover, because the elderly man knew of the danger but did not warn the neighbor.
choices.D: The neighbor should recover, because there is privity between lessor and lessee and it cannot be broken unilaterally.

questions.explanation:
Dangerous conditions on land
(landlord's duties)
  • Warn tenant of known latent (hidden) defects on land
  • Safely perform repairs
  • Ensure common areas are in safe condition
  • Maintain areas necessary for safe use of land (eg, walls, roof)
  • Keep land in good repair (lease provision required)
  • Protect entrants from dangerous condition on land leased for public purpose

Landlords have no duty to warn tenants about dangerous conditions on the premises unless those conditions are latent. Dangerous latent defects are conditions that:

  • the landlord knows, or should know, pose an unreasonable risk of physical harm
  • exist when the tenant takes possession and
  • could not be discovered by the tenant's reasonable inspection.

A landlord who breaches this duty is liable for physical harm caused by the condition—even after the landlord conveys the leased property to another.

Here, the elderly man knew that the barn wall was dangerously weakened by rot when the neighbor took possession. Since the neighbor's inspection of the barn would not have revealed the rot (only an engineer would have found it), the man had a duty to warn the neighbor about the wall. The man failed to do so and is therefore liable for the neighbor's injuries—even after conveying the barn to his granddaughter.

(Choice A) The neighbor's failure to inspect the barn is of no consequence because he could not have discovered the defect upon inspection.

(Choice B) Attornment occurs when a tenant accepts a new landlord in place of an old one. However, the new landlord does not become liable for dangerous latent defects until he/she has had a reasonable opportunity to discover and take effective precautions against them. Here, just one day had passed since the barn was conveyed to the granddaughter, so she had no reasonable opportunity to discover the defect.

(Choice D) There is privity of contract (shared interest under the lease) and privity of estate (successive rights to possess the property) between a lessor and lessee. Privity of estate can be broken unilaterally when either party conveys his/her entire interest under the lease, but privity of contract cannot. And though privity may create a duty, the neighbor cannot recover unless he also shows that duty was breached.

📌 Educational Objective

A landlord must warn a tenant about dangerous latent conditions that

  • the landlord knows, or should know, pose an unreasonable risk of physical harm,
  • exist when the tenant takes possession, and
  • could not be discovered by reasonable inspection.
📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Property § 17.1, cmt. l (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (landlord's liability for latent defects following a transfer of the landlord's interest).
questions.zh-question:
一位老人将一个谷仓租给他的邻居，租期为三年。邻居占有了该谷仓并将其用于农事用途。租赁合同规定，老人负责谷仓的结构性维修，除非维修是由邻居的行为所致。

一年后，老人将谷仓及其相关土地转让给他的孙女，并注明“须遵守与我邻居的租赁合同”。邻居将下个月的租金支付给了孙女。第二天，谷仓的一段外墙因墙体内部结构腐烂而倒塌。这面墙表面上看起来很坚固，但一位称职的工程师在检查后本可以发现其状况。孙女和邻居都没有请工程师检查过谷仓。邻居因墙体倒塌而受伤。

老人在邻居占有谷仓时，就知道墙体已因腐烂而变得危险且需要立即维修，但他没有告知邻居或其孙女。本案没有适用的成文法。

邻居对老人提起了适当的诉讼，要求赔偿其所受的伤害。孙女不是本案当事人。

关于本案的结果，以下哪项评论最为恰当？

zh-choices.A: 邻居应该败诉，因为他未能检查谷仓。
zh-choices.B: 邻居应该败诉，因为邻居向孙女履行“attornment”（承认新地主）后，孙女承担了老人的所有义务。
zh-choices.C: 邻居应该获得赔偿，因为老人知道危险但没有警告邻居。
zh-choices.D: 邻居应该获得赔偿，因为出租人和承租人之间存在法律上的利害关系（privity），且该关系不能被单方面破坏。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Tort Liabilities

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：房东明知承租时就存在的隐蔽危险缺陷，却没有警告，后来即使把房子转给孙女，自己仍可能要对承租人的人身损害负责。

三秒认题路径：

已知危险 → 隐蔽缺陷 → 交付时存在 → 未告知 → 房东赔

核心法律规则

只看这条就够了

房东（landlord）对隐蔽危险缺陷（latent dangerous defect）有警告义务，考场意思：房东知道或应知该缺陷、缺陷在承租人接管时就已经存在、而且靠合理检查发现不了。

如果房东违反这个义务，之后把租赁物业转出去，也usually逃不掉对因此发生的人身损害（physical harm）责任。考试上这题只问：老房东自己有没有先违约，而不是孙女后来会不会接锅。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Property § 17.1 的规则直接锁定结论：转让后，原房东对既有的隐蔽危险仍可负责。

思维导图

先问：这是“房东对隐蔽危险缺陷”的责任题吗？
事实钩子老人明知墙内有腐烂，且工程师才看得出。
规则门槛承租时已存在 + 合理检查发现不了 + 房东知道或应知。
直接结论房东当时就有警告义务，没警告就是违约。
再问：转给孙女后，原房东就脱身了吗？
杀题点不能。转让不抹掉先前对隐蔽危险的违约。
别被带偏这里不是在考“谁现在是新房东”，而是在考“谁先没告知已存在的危险”。
答案落点邻居可向原房东索赔，选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：邻居没有请工程师检查，应该自己承担后果。

但考试真正问的是：这个缺陷是不是本来就藏着，而且普通检查看不出来；如果看不出来，房东先前的警告义务不会因为“没查”就消失。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干老人早就知道墙内腐烂且未警告，而普通检查发现不了，所以他对邻居的伤害要负责，转给孙女也不洗掉这次违约。

❌ 事实误判 | 误认可发现

✕ A: 把reasonable inspection看成能查出。

❌ 法律适用 | 错套承租转移

✕ B: 误把扭转租约当成孙女立刻接手旧房东责任。

❌ 概念混淆 | 把 privity 当万能

✕ D: 以为privity一在就必赢，忽略先前已违约。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“已知的隐蔽危险”，再看“是否可由合理检查发现”，最后别被后续转让带跑。

考场速记

记住一句：承租时已存在、房东知道、普通检查查不出，就先锁定原房东责任；后面转让给谁，通常不影响这次没警告的后果。

reason.en: Establishes the landlord-tenant relationship that triggers the lessor's duties.

B.text: assumed all of the elderly man's obligations

C.text: knew of the danger but did not warn

label.zh: 出租人与承租人之间的相对关系

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A woman conveyed a vacant rural lot by a warranty deed that stated: "to my daughter for life, and upon her death, to my heirs." The next year, the woman executed a quitclaim deed for the same lot to the daughter with the expressed intent "to make absolute" the interest granted to her.
Four years later, the daughter and her newborn child were involved in a car accident and sustained serious injuries. To pay for their medical expenses, the daughter sold the lot to a real estate developer. The daughter died several months later, leaving the child as her sole heir.
The child's legal representative has asked a lawyer for advice regarding ownership of the lot. There is no applicable statute.
Who should the lawyer say is the owner of the lot?

choices.A: The child, because the child is the woman's sole heir.
choices.B: The child, because the child received a remainder following the daughter's life estate.
choices.C: The developer, because the daughter acquired fee simple title upon the execution of the quitclaim deed.
choices.D: The developer, because the warranty deed conveyed fee simple title to the daughter.

questions.explanation:
Present interest
Future interest
Woman's
warranty deed
“to daughter for life”
daughter = life estate
“then to my heirs”
woman = reversion
(Doctrine of Worthier Title)
Woman's
quitclaim deed
“to daughter in absolute”
daughter = reversion
daughter = fee simple absolute
(Merger rule)
Daughter's sale
developer = fee simple absolute

The doctrine of worthier title is triggered when a grantor conveys property inter vivos to another and, in the same instrument, conveys a future interest to the grantor's heirs. When this occurs, the future interest is rendered void and the grantor is deemed to hold a reversion. Most states have abolished this doctrine by statute, but there is no applicable statute in this jurisdiction. Therefore, the woman's warranty deed conveyed a life estate to the daughter and a reversion to the woman—not a remainder to her heirs (Choices B & D).

The woman then conveyed her reversion to the daughter via quitclaim deed—leaving no other interest in the lot for the woman's heirs (Choice A). This means that the daughter held both a present interest (life estate) and future interest (the woman's reversion) in the lot with no intervening interest. As a result, the daughter's two interests merged into a fee simple absolute under the doctrine of merger. And since the daughter subsequently conveyed that interest to the developer, the lawyer should say that the developer owns the lot.

📌 Educational Objective

The doctrine of worthier title applies when a grantor makes an inter vivos conveyance to another with a future interest to the grantor's heirs. The future interest is then deemed to create a reversion in the grantor—not a remainder in the grantor's heirs.
questions.zh-question:
一名女性通过一份担保契据转让了一块空置的乡村地块，契据规定："授予我的女儿终身持有，待其亡故后，归我的继承人所有。"

次年，该女性就同一地块向其女儿签署了一份放弃权利契据，明确意图是使其授予的权益“绝对化”。

四年后，女儿和她刚出生的孩子遭遇车祸，身受重伤。为支付医疗费用，女儿将该地块出售给了一位房地产开发商。

几个月后，女儿去世，留下孩子作为其唯一继承人。

孩子的法定代理人就该地块的所有权问题咨询了一位律师。本案没有适用的成文法。

律师应该说谁是该地块的所有人？

zh-choices.A: 孩子，因为孩子是该女性的唯一继承人。
zh-choices.B: 孩子，因为在女儿的终身地产权之后，孩子获得了剩余地产权。
zh-choices.C: 开发商，因为女儿在放弃权利契据签署后获得了完全所有权。
zh-choices.D: 开发商，因为担保契据将完全所有权转让给了女儿。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Future interests

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：先看 doctrine of worthier title（较优权源原则）把“给继承人”的那句话打回 reversion（回返权益），再看女儿拿到两个无中间人利益后会不会 merge（合并）成 fee simple absolute（完全所有权）。

三秒认题路径：

给继承人 → 先转回返 → 女儿再拿到 → 两权合并 → 开发商赢

核心法律规则

doctrine of worthier title（较优权源原则）考场意思：生前转让里如果把未来权益写给“我的继承人”，很多州会把这句当成无效，改判成出让人自己保留 reversion（回返权益）。

这里题干说“to my heirs”，所以不是女儿的 remainder（余留权）；而是女人自己先留了回返权益。随后女人又把这项回返权益用 quitclaim deed（放弃权契据）给了女儿，女儿手里就同时握有现在的 life estate（终身地产）和未来的回返权益，中间没有第三人插着。

这种情况下会触发 merger（合并规则）：女儿把两个利益合成 fee simple absolute（完全所有权），之后她卖给开发商，开发商就拿到完整产权。

核心判例： Doctrine of Worthier Title 规则锁定：同一份生前转让里给“继承人”的未来权益，通常不算继承人的余留权，而是出让人的回返权益。

思维导图

女人 契据原始出让人
→
女儿 先拿 life estate
→
女人“继承人” 这句先被打回 reversion
→
女儿再受让回返权益 手里凑齐两个利益
先看：同一份生前契据里写“to my heirs”吗？
是： 触发 worthier title，继承人的“未来权”不保留。
卡死点：不是女儿的 remainder，而是女人的 reversion。
再看： 女人后来是否把 reversion 给了女儿？
是 → 女儿同时持有 life estate + reversion。
最后： 无中间人插着时，两个利益 merge。
结论：女儿变成 fee simple absolute，再卖给开发商，开发商拿到完整产权。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：题干写了“to my heirs”，那女儿是不是只拿到终身地，剩下给孩子？

但考试真正问的是：这句在 worthier title 下先不算给继承人的余留权，而是回到女人自己的 reversion；后来女儿再把它和自己的终身地合并，所以孩子不是被直接传到的那一位。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上谁有产权」，不是「故事里谁最像该继承的人」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

女儿后来通过 quitclaim deed 拿到女人的 reversion，与原本的 life estate 合并成 fee simple absolute，所以她卖给开发商时能转出完整产权。

❌ 事实误判 | 误认继承来源

✕ A: 把 sole heir 当成直接得房，忽略女儿早已把完整产权卖掉了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 余留权误认

✕ B: 把“to my heirs”当成孩子的 remainder，漏掉 worthier title 先把它改成回返权益。

❌ 法律适用 | 契据效果错套

✕ D: 只看到 warranty deed，却没算后来那份 quitclaim 已经把权利链补完整。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓契据里的未来权益怎么定性，再查后续转让有没有把两个利益合并成完全所有权。

考场速记

记住一句：“to my heirs” 在很多州先别急着当余留权，先想 worthier title，再问后面有没有 merger。这题的顺序就是：先打回回返权益，再看谁最后拿到完整产权。

reason.en: Creates only a life estate in the daughter, not fee simple.

B.text: remainder following the daughter's life estate

D.text: warranty deed conveyed fee simple title

highlights.text: to my daughter for life, and upon her death, to my heirs

reason.en: Sets up life estate plus a future interest that worthier title converts to a reversion.
reason.zh: 创设终身地产及未来权益，更优产权原则将其转化为归复权。

highlights.text: There is no applicable statute.

reason.en: Preserves common-law worthier title instead of a statutory abolition.
reason.zh: 保留普通法下的更优产权原则，而非成文法废除。

highlights.text: quitclaim deed for the same lot to the daughter with the expressed intent "to make absolute"

reason.en: Transfers the woman's reversion so merger can create fee simple in the daughter.
reason.zh: 转让女人的归复权，使合并原则可在女儿处形成完全保有地产。

highlights.text: The daughter sold the lot to a real estate developer.

reason.en: Determines who owns the lot after the merged fee simple is conveyed.
reason.zh: 决定合并后的完全保有地产转让后谁拥有该土地。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A brother and sister were jointly in possession of land in fee simple as tenants in common. They joined in a mortgage of the land to a bank. The brother erected a fence along what he considered to be the true boundary between the land and the adjoining property, owned by the neighbor. Shortly thereafter, the brother had an argument with the sister and gave up his possession of the land. The debt secured by the mortgage had not been paid.
The neighbor surveyed his land and found that the fence erected a year earlier by the brother did not follow the true boundary. Part of the fence was within the brother and sister's land. Part of the fence encroached on the neighbor's land. The neighbor and the sister executed an agreement fixing the boundary line in accordance with the fence constructed by the brother. The agreement, which met all the formalities required in the jurisdiction, was promptly and properly recorded.
A year after the agreement was recorded, the brother temporarily reconciled his differences with the sister and resumed joint possession of the land. Thereafter, the brother repudiated the boundary-line agreement and brought an appropriate action against the neighbor and the sister to quiet title along the original true boundary.
In such action, will the brother prevail?

choices.A: No, because the agreement, as a matter of law, was mutually beneficial to the brother and sister.
choices.B: No, because the sister was in sole possession of the land at the time the agreement was signed.
choices.C: Yes, because one tenant in common cannot bind another tenant in common to a boundary-line agreement.
choices.D: Yes, because the bank was not a party to the agreement.

questions.explanation:
Consent between cotenants in common
(common examples)
Consent required No consent required
  • Convey entire co-owned property
  • Obtain exclusive possession over part of property
  • Bind other cotenants' interests in contract with third party
  • Sell, lease, or devise personal ownership interest
  • Possess entire co-owned property
  • Extract minerals from co-owned property (unless committing waste)

Tenancy in common is concurrent ownership of land where each co-tenant has a share of the property but an equal right to possess the whole property (ie, separate but undivided interests). A co-tenant may transfer his/her own interest without the other co-tenants' consent. However, a co-tenant cannot transfer other co-tenants' interests or bind them under a contract affecting the property (eg, a boundary-line agreement).

Here, the brother and sister share the land in fee simple as tenants in common. The sister and the neighbor executed a contract fixing the boundary line in accordance with a fence erected by the brother. Although the brother was not in possession of the land at the time the agreement was signed, he was still a co-tenant (Choice B). Therefore, the sister could not bind him to that agreement, and he will likely prevail.

(Choice A) When a contract is mutually beneficial to all co-tenants, it is presumed that they have all ratified (ie, confirmed or accepted) the contract. And though ratification renders an otherwise invalid contract valid, a presumed ratification is rebutted when a co-tenant repudiates the agreement (as seen here).

(Choice D) Under the lien theory of mortgages (majority rule), a lender has a security interest - but not title - in the mortgaged property.

Therefore, the fact that the bank was not a party to the boundary-line agreement does not render it unenforceable against the brother. Instead, the brother is not bound because he was not a party.

📌 Educational Objective

Although a tenant in common may freely transfer his/her interest to a third party, that tenant cannot transfer another co-tenant's interest or bind another co-tenant to a contract affecting the shared property.

📚 References
  • 20 Am. Jur. 2d Cotenancy and Joint Ownership § 93 (2018) (ability to bind other co-tenants).
questions.zh-question:
一对兄妹作为共同共有人（tenants in common），以完全所有权（fee simple）的方式共同占有一块土地。他们共同将该土地抵押给一家银行。哥哥沿着他认为是该土地与邻居拥有的相邻地产之间的真实边界竖立了一道栅栏。此后不久，哥哥与妹妹发生争执，并放弃了他对该土地的占有。该抵押所担保的债务尚未偿还。

邻居勘测了他的土地，发现哥哥一年前竖立的栅栏并未遵循真实边界。部分栅栏在兄妹的土地范围内，部分栅栏侵占了邻居的土地。邻居和妹妹签订了一份协议，根据哥哥建造的栅栏来确定边界线。该协议符合该司法管辖区要求的所有正式手续，并被及时且妥善地进行了登记。

协议登记一年后，哥哥与妹妹暂时和解，并恢复了对该土地的共同占有。此后，哥哥否认了该边界线协议，并对邻居和妹妹提起了适当的诉讼，要求沿着原始的真实边界进行产权确认（quiet title）。

在此诉讼中，哥哥会胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为从法律上讲，该协议对兄妹双方都有利。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为在签署协议时，妹妹是该土地的唯一占有人。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为一个共同共有人（tenant in common）不能以一份边界线协议约束另一位共同共有人。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为银行不是该协议的一方。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Concurrent estates

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：共有不分割产权（tenancy in common）里，一个共有人不能把另一个共有人绑进影响共有土地的合同，所以妹妹签的边界协议不能直接约束哥哥。

三秒认题路径：

共有关系 → 一方签约 → 绑到他人？ → 不能 → 哥哥赢

核心法律规则

在共有不分割产权（tenancy in common）中，每个共有人都能处分自己的份额，但不能替别的共有人处分他们的份额，也不能单方把别人绑进一个影响共有土地的合同里。边界协议（boundary-line agreement）如果是由一个共有人单独签的，通常只对签字的人有效，不会自动约束没签字的共有人。

这里哥哥虽然当时暂时离开了土地，但他仍然是共有人，所以妹妹不能靠自己和邻居的协议把哥哥的权利一起改掉。考试上你要记住：ownership 可以各自处分，binding another cotenant 不行。

核心判例： 本题考的是共有人能否替他人作出会影响共有土地的约定；规则直接锁定结论：不能。

思维导图

先看：这是在问“一个共有人签的边界协议，能不能绑住另一个共有人”吗？
YES 轨道：土地是tenancy in common → 妹妹与邻居单独定界 → 这类合同会影响共有地 → 关键是能否代表哥哥
规则门槛：共有人能处分自己的份额，但不能转让别人的份额，也不能单方绑定别的共有人
卡死点：哥哥没签字，只是后来回到土地上，并不等于同意那份边界协议
排除误导：是否当时不在场？不是关键；银行是否参与？也不是关键
结论：妹妹不能替哥哥定边界 → 哥哥可以挑战协议 → 选 C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：妹妹和邻居都签了、而且还是按照篱笆线定界，看起来很“合理”，好像哥哥后来回来也该一起受影响。

但考试真正问的是：一个共有人能不能单独把别的共有人绑进影响共有土地的协议里。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

所以别被“哥哥后来回来了”或“协议看起来对大家有利”带跑；这题的核心不是公平感，而是谁有签约权。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干里真正的决定点是：妹妹单独和邻居签边界协议，但哥哥仍是共有人，所以她不能替哥哥绑定这份会改共有土地范围的合同。

❌ 概念混淆 | 共同受益误判

✕ A: 看到“对双方有利”就想当然以为哥哥也被算进去。

❌ 事实误判 | 误抓占有状态

✕ B: 哥哥当时没占有，不等于他失去共有人身份。

❌ 法律适用 | 牵错银行责任

✕ D: bank not a party 不是关键，问题在于哥哥根本没同意。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认共有关系，再问“谁签字、谁被绑定”，不要被邻居、银行和占有细节带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：共有不分割产权（tenancy in common）里，能转自己的份额，不能替别人签约。碰到“一个共有人单独和第三人改共有地边界、租赁或处分”的题，先问：没签字的共有人有没有真的被绑定？通常没有。

这题的快捷口诀：“自己份额自己管，别人的权利别乱签。”

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A landowner conveyed his land by quitclaim deed to his daughter and son "as joint tenants in fee simple." The language of the deed was sufficient to create a common law joint tenancy with right of survivorship, which is unmodified by statute.
The daughter then duly executed a will devising her interest in the land to a friend. Then the son duly executed a will devising his interest in the land to a cousin.
The son died, and later the daughter died. Neither had ever married. The daughter's friend and the cousin survived.
After both wills have been duly probated, who owns what interest in the land?

choices.A: The cousin owns the fee simple.
choices.B: The daughter's friend and the cousin own equal shares as joint tenants with right of survivorship.
choices.C: The daughter's friend and the cousin own equal shares as tenants in common.
choices.D: The daughter's friend owns the fee simple.

questions.explanation:
Joint tenancy with right of survivorship

Joint tenants
Tenant A
Tenant B
Tenant A dies
(interest absorbed)
Surviving tenant
Tenant B
right of possession ownership interest

A joint tenancy is a type of concurrent estate同时共有产权：两人或以上在同一时间对不动产拥有未分割权益的共有形式。 in which each co-tenant has an undivided and equal interest in the property with the right of survivorship. The right of survivorship means that a joint tenant's interest disappears upon his/her death and the remaining joint tenants' interests automatically expand to absorb it. Therefore, a joint tenant has no interest to devise upon death.

Here, the daughter and the son were joint tenants in fee simple. Although they executed wills attempting to devise their joint tenancy interests to others, they could not do so because of their right of survivorship. But the joint tenancy disappeared when the son died, and the daughter automatically acquired the entire property in fee simple. As a result, her fee simple interest passed to the friend under her will when she died.

(Choice A) Since the son was a joint tenant and died first, his property interest was acquired by the daughter. As a result, the son had no interest to devise to his cousin under a will.

(Choice B) Under the common law and in most jurisdictions, a joint tenancy with right of survivorship entails four unities四个统一体（four unities）：普通法上创设联权共有所需的四项统一要件，包括时间、产权、利益与占有的统一。. This includes unity of title, which requires joint tenants to receive their interests in the same instrument of conveyance. Since the friend and the cousin received their purported interests in separate wills, they could not acquire joint tenancy interests.

(Choice C) A lifetime transfer of a joint tenant's interest severs that interest from the joint tenancy, and it becomes a tenancy-in-common ownership interest. Therefore, the friend and cousin would have owned equal shares of the property as tenants in common had the daughter and son conveyed their interests when they were alive instead of attempting to devise them at death.

📌 Educational Objective

A joint tenant's interest disappears upon his/her death and the remaining joint tenants' interests automatically expand to absorb it (ie, right of survivorship). Therefore, a joint tenancy interest cannot be devised.
questions.zh-question:
一位土地所有者通过一份免责契据（quitclaim deed）将其土地转让给他的女儿和儿子，“作为享有完全保有地产权（fee simple）的联权共有人（joint tenants）”。该契据的措辞足以创设普通法上附带生存者权（right of survivorship）的联权共有关系，且该关系未经成文法修改。

随后，女儿依合法程序订立了一份遗嘱，将其在该土地上的权益遗赠给一位朋友。然后，儿子也依合法程序订立了一份遗嘱，将其在该土地上的权益遗赠给一位堂/表亲。

儿子去世，之后女儿也去世了。两人均未曾结婚。女儿的朋友和该堂/表亲均在世。

在两份遗嘱都经过合法的遗嘱认证程序后，谁对该土地拥有何种权益？

zh-choices.A: 堂/表亲拥有完全保有地产权（fee simple）。
zh-choices.B: 女儿的朋友和堂/表亲作为附带生存者权（right of survivorship）的联权共有人（joint tenants），拥有平等的份额。
zh-choices.C: 女儿的朋友和堂/表亲作为分权共有人（tenants in common），拥有平等的份额。
zh-choices.D: 女儿的朋友拥有完全保有地产权（fee simple）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Concurrent estates

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：联权共有（joint tenancy）带有生存者取得权（right of survivorship），所以死亡的一方不能再用遗嘱处分自己的份额，最后活着的人直接拿到整块地。

三秒认题路径：

联权共有 → 一方先死 → 份额吸收 → 不能遗嘱处分 → 终局归幸存者

核心法律规则

联权共有（joint tenancy）的核心是两点：各共有人持有不分割的平等权益，而且带有生存者取得权（right of survivorship）。考试上的意思很直接：一个联权共有人一死，他那一份不是“留给继承人”，而是立刻被其他联权共有人吸收。

所以，joint tenancy 里的份额在死亡时已经消失，死亡者手里没有可遗赠的财产可写进遗嘱。若只剩一人活着，这个人就把整块地变成自己的fee simple。

核心判例： 本题对应的是 joint tenancy 的普通法规则：死亡会切断被继承人的份额，幸存者自动吸收，因此死亡时不能再 devise。

思维导图

共同取得 同一份契约写入
→
联权共有 有 survivorship
→
先死一人 其份额消失
→
幸存者吸收 自动扩张为全额
→
不能遗嘱处分 死时无可devise的份额
题干钩子：先看是不是 joint tenancy，再看谁先死。
关键点 先死的那个人，其权益已经被吸收，遗嘱对这份权益无效。
卡死结论：最后活着的女儿拿到整块 fee simple，随后再按她的遗嘱给 friend。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：儿子先死，他的份额应该按遗嘱给 cousin；女儿后死，她也可以把自己的份额留给 friend。

但考试真正问的是：joint tenancy 的份额会不会在死亡时自动消失并被幸存者吸收。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能处分」，而不是「你主观上想不想把它留给别人」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干已给出 joint tenants in fee simple，儿子先死后其份额被女儿吸收；女儿死时才有完整 fee simple 可遗赠给 friend。

❌ 事实误判 | 先死份额偷换

✕ A: 把 first to die 当成还能留下财产，其实儿子的份额当场被女儿吸收了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 遗嘱联权混用

✕ B: 以为 friend 和 cousin 能靠两份遗嘱凑成 joint tenants，但联权共有不靠遗嘱拼出来。

❌ 法律适用 | 共有转换误套

✕ C: 把生前转让后的 tenants in common 规则搬来这里，但题干只有死后遗嘱，没有生前转让。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓所有权类型，再问死亡时份额还在不在；还在才谈遗嘱，不在就直接让 survivorship 说话。

考场速记

记住一句：联权共有（joint tenancy）里，死亡先发生的人没有遗嘱可处分的份额，因为份额会被幸存者自动吸收。下次看到“joint tenants”四个字，先默念：survivorship beats devise。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A mother owned a two-family apartment house on a small city lot not suitable for partition-in-kind. Upon the mother's death, her will devised the apartment house to "my two sons, in equal shares."
A week ago, a creditor obtained a money judgment against the youngest son and properly filed the judgment in the county where the apartment house is located. A statute in the jurisdiction provides: "Any judgment properly filed shall, for ten years from filing, be a lien on the real property then owned or subsequently acquired by any person against whom the judgment is rendered."
The youngest son needed cash, but the oldest son did not wish to sell the apartment house. Nevertheless, the youngest son commenced a partition action against the oldest son and the creditor. The court properly ordered a partition by judicial sale.
After the sale, the creditor's judgment will be a lien on what interest?

choices.A: All of the apartment house.
choices.B: All of the proceeds of sale of the apartment house.
choices.C: Only a one-half interest in the apartment house.
choices.D: Only the portion of the proceeds of sale due to the youngest son.

questions.explanation:
Attachment of lien after partition
Is creditor a party to debtor's partition action?
No
Interest remains on debtor's property interest.
Yes
How is property partitioned?
In kind (physical division)
Interest remains on debtor's property interest.
By sale (monetary division)
Interest attaches to debtor's proceeds from sale.

Co-tenantsCo-tenants（共同共有人）：两人或以上对不动产享有同时、可分割权益的共有关系，如按份共有。 can freely encumber their separate interests in the property without consent of the other tenants (except in a tenancy by the entirety). This means that a tenant can use his/her share of the property to secure repayment of a debt, and creditors will only have a lien on that tenant's property interest. And if any tenant later seeks to divide the property through a partitionPartition（分割）：共有人请求法院将共有财产在共有人之间进行实物分割或变价分割的法律程序。 by sale, that lien will either:

  • remain on the tenant-debtor's property interest if the creditor is not a party to the partition action or
  • attach to the tenant-debtor's share of proceeds from the sale if the creditor is a party to the partition action.

Here, the two sons became co-tenants when the mother devised them a duplex in equal shares. A creditor later obtained and filed a money judgment against the youngest son, creating a judgment lien on his one-half interest in the duplex. The youngest son then commenced an action for partition by sale against the oldest son and the creditor—which the court granted. Since the creditor was a party to the partition action, the judgment lien will attach to the youngest son's portion of the proceeds from the judicial sale (Choices A, B & C).

📌 Educational Objective

When a co-tenancy is divided in an action for partition by sale, any lien on a tenant's property interest will stay attached to that interest if the creditor is not a party to the action. But if the creditor is a party, then the lien will attach to the sale proceeds attributable to that interest.
questions.zh-question:
一位母亲在城市的一小块地块上拥有一栋双户公寓楼，该地块不适合进行实物分割。

母亲去世后，其遗嘱将该公寓楼遗赠给“我的两个儿子，平等享有份额。”

一周前，一名债权人获得了针对小儿子的金钱判决，并在该公寓楼所在的郡县妥善登记了该判决。该司法管辖区的一项法规规定：“任何妥善登记的判决，自登记之日起十年内，均构成对被判决人当时拥有或此后获得的不动产的留置权。”

小儿子需要现金，但大儿子不希望出售该公寓楼。然而，小儿子对大儿子和该债权人提起了分割之诉。法院依法下令通过司法出售进行分割。

出售后，债权人的判决将对何种权益构成留置权？

zh-choices.A: 公寓楼的全部。
zh-choices.B: 公寓楼销售所得的全部款项。
zh-choices.C: 仅公寓楼一半的权益。
zh-choices.D: 仅销售所得款中应归属于小儿子的那一部分。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Concurrent estates

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：共有人被法院司法变价分割（partition by sale）后，判决留置权（judgment lien）到底跟着房子本身走，还是改挂到卖房价款上。

三秒认题路径：

共有人 → 变价分割 → 债权人参加 → 留置权转到价款 → 选 D

核心法律规则

共有人可以单独处分自己的份额，所以债权人通常只对该共有人自己的财产权份额（property interest）设留置权，考场意思：不会一下子压到整栋楼。

但如果后来进入分割诉讼（partition action），而债权人本身也是当事人，那么在司法变价分割（partition by sale）里，这个留置权会跟着该份额对应的卖房价款（proceeds）走，而不是继续卡在原房产上。

反过来，如果债权人不是分割案当事人，留置权才会继续附着在原来的财产权份额上。

核心判例： 本题不需要特定判例名，抓住考点就是：partition by sale + 债权人是当事人 → 留置权转到该共有人对应的价款。

思维导图

先问：债权人是不是分割诉讼的当事人？
否留置权继续挂在该共有人原本的财产权份额上
是再看：法院怎么分？
实物分割留置权仍附着在原财产权份额上
变价分割留置权改附着在该共有人应得的卖房价款上
本题事实：债权人是当事人 + 变价分割 → 结论：只盯 youngest son 的那一半价款

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然已经对房子设了留置权，那卖掉以后就该整栋房子的价款都被它抓住。

但考试真正问的是：这个 lien 只追到债务人那一份，而且在债权人参加分割案、法院又作司法变价分割（partition by sale）时，它转挂到该份额对应的价款，不是去吞掉另一位共有人那一半。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干已经写明债权人参加了分割案，又是partition by sale；所以留置权不再挂在房子上，而是挂到 youngest son 应得的卖房价款上。

❌ 事实误判 | 夸大留置范围

✕ A: 把留置权偷扩大到整栋房子，忽略它本来只追债务人那份。

❌ 法律适用 | 价款全吞误判

✕ B: 以为卖房后所有价款都被 lien 锁死，忽略只跟债务人份额走。

❌ 概念混淆 | 份额与整物混淆

✕ C: 还把 lien 当成压在整套房子上，其实只附在 youngest son 的半份权益上。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定“债权人是否参加分割案”，再看“实物分割还是变价分割”，最后把 lien 挂到正确标的上。

考场速记

记忆口诀：分割看当事人，变价看价款。债权人参加并且法院卖房时，留置权就跟着债务人那份价款走，不会继续压整栋房子。
