questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
An individual who was domiciled in State A throughout her life deeded land in State A to a charity organized under the laws of State B but retained a right of entry if the land was not used for a charitable purpose. Later in her life, the individual transferred the right of entry to a creditor. The individual then devised her entire estate to her son shortly before she died. Recently, the charity ceased to use the land for a charitable purpose. The son and the creditor are domiciled in State B.
The law of State A, adhering to the common law, does not permit an inter vivos transfer of a right of entry. The law of State B permits a right of entry to be transferred during the owner's life.
The son has initiated a lawsuit in a state court in State B seeking a declaratory judgment that he is the owner of the land and naming the charity and the creditor as parties in this action.
Is the court likely to rule in the son's favor?

choices.A: No, because the court in State B must apply the law of State B.
choices.B: No, because the parties to this action are domiciled in State B.
choices.C: Yes, because the individual was domiciled in State A throughout her life.
choices.D: Yes, because the law of State A likely governs this matter.

questions.explanation:
Conflict-of-laws rule for real property issues
General rule In cases involving real property, law applied by forum court should be determined by conflict-of-laws rule that would be applied by state where property is located
Exceptions
  • Document specifies application of specific jurisdiction's laws
  • Issues regarding effect of marriage on interest in land
  • Collateral issues (eg, whether transferor perpetrated fraud)
  • Issues regarding mortgage note (eg, validity of note)
  • Foreclosure-related issues that do not affect interest in land (eg, mortgagee's right to sue mortgagor for underlying debt before foreclosure)

A conflict-of-laws issue arises when significant aspects of a legal action are divided between two or more states and there is a conflict as to which state's law applies (as seen here). If such a conflict arises in a case involving real property, the general conflict-of-laws rule is as follows:

The law applied by the forum court should be determined by the conflict-of-laws rule that would be applied by the courts of the situs state—ie, the state where the property is located.

The conflict-of-laws rule of the situs state typically directs the application of its own local law on that issue (ie, the law of the situs) in resolving the matter.

Here, the land is located in State A, so the law of State A (law of the situs) likely governs this matter. Since the law of State A does not permit an inter vivos transfer of a right of entry, the individual could not transfer her right of entry to the creditor during her lifetime. Instead, it passed to her son under her will. Therefore, the State B court will likely rule in the son's favor (Choice A).

(Choice B) The fact that the parties to this action are domiciled in State B shows that the State B court has personal jurisdiction over them. But this does not determine which state's law governs the matter.

(Choice C) Although the individual was domiciled in State A throughout her life, the situs of the property (not the domicile of the transferor) determines the law to be applied in this matter.

📌 Educational Objective

When there is a conflict-of-laws issue in a case involving real property, the general rule is that the applicable law should be determined by the conflict-of-laws rule of the state where the property is located (ie, situs state). This usually results in the application of the situs state's local law on that issue.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Conflict of Laws § 223 (Am. Law Inst. 1971) (validity and effect of conveyance of interest in land).

一名终身居住在A州的个人，将其位于A州的土地通过契约转让给一家根据B州法律成立的慈善机构，但保留了一项进入权，即如果该土地不被用于慈善目的，她有权进入并收回土地。在其晚年，该个人将此进入权转让给了一名债权人。随后，该个人在去世前不久，通过遗嘱将其全部遗产遗赠给了她的儿子。最近，该慈善机构停止将该土地用于慈善目的。其儿子和债权人均居住在B州。

A州的法律遵循普通法，不允许生前转让（inter vivos transfer）进入权。B州的法律则允许在所有者生前转让进入权。

儿子已在B州的一家州法院提起诉讼，请求宣告性判决（declaratory judgment），确认他是该土地的所有人，并将该慈善机构和债权人列为本案当事人。

法院是否可能做出有利于儿子的裁决？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为B州的法院必须适用B州的法律。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为本案当事人的居住地在B州。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该个人终身居住在A州。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为A州的法律很可能管辖此事。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Special Real Property Issues

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：土地相关权利到底该跟着谁的法走，重点是看不动产所在地法（situs law），不是看当事人住在哪个州。

三秒认题路径：

地在A州 → 先看situs → 适用A州法 → 右回归不能生前转让 → 继承给儿子

核心法律规则

一眼抓住的规则

涉及不动产（real property）的争议，论坛法院先按物所在地州（situs state）自己的冲突规范来选法，考试上通常还是落回该州的本地法。这里真正管用的是土地坐落州的法，不是转让人或当事人的住所（domicile）。

本题的土地在State A，所以应优先适用State A法；而State A不允许生前转让（inter vivos transfer）回归权（right of entry），所以这项权利不能有效转给债权人。结果就是，这项权利仍会按遗嘱走，题目里儿子更可能赢。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Conflict of Laws § 223 - 不动产利益的效力与转让，通常由物所在地法决定。

思维导图

题干先看
土地在 State A
→
触发规则
不动产争议
→
situs state 先选物所在地州的冲突规范
→
再落回本地法
State A law
→
关键卡点
right of entry 不能生前转让
→
结论
权利归儿子，State B 不是答案

考点陷阱

你可能会想：被告都住在State B，那就该用State B法。

但考试真正问的是：哪一州的法决定土地权利效力，不是哪一州方便起诉。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

土地在State A，所以冲突法指向State A法；又因为State A不许right of entry生前转让，债权人拿不到这项权利，儿子更可能胜诉。

❌ 法律适用 | 州法直套误判

✕ A: 误以为一定直接管土地权利，忽略了situs规则。

❌ 事实误判 | 住所当成选法

✕ B: 把domiciled in State B当成选法依据了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 住所优先误判

✕ C: 盯着转让人一生住哪州，却忘了看土地坐落在哪州。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定不动产所在地，再判断该州法是否允许权利生前转让。

考场速记

记忆口诀：土地看所在地，不是看人住哪里。碰到不动产冲突法，先问“situs州怎么选法”，再看本地法怎么定权利归属。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A husband and wife acquired land as common law joint tenants with right of survivorship. One year later, without his wife's knowledge, the husband executed a will devising his interest in the land to his best friend. The husband subsequently died.
Is the wife now the sole owner of the land?

choices.A: No, because a joint tenant has the unilateral right to end a joint tenancy without the consent of the other joint tenant.
choices.B: No, because the wife's interest in the husband's undivided 50% ownership in the land adeemed.
choices.C: Yes, because of the doctrine of after-acquired title, or estoppel by deed.
choices.D: Yes, because the devise to the friend did not sever the joint tenancy.

questions.explanation:
Joint tenancy with right of survivorship

Joint tenants
Tenant A
Tenant B
Tenant A dies
(interest absorbed)
Surviving tenant
Tenant B
right of possession ownership interest

A joint tenancy is a type of concurrent estate同时共有产权：两人或以上在同一时间对不动产拥有未分割权益的共有形式。 in which each co-tenant has an undivided and equal interest in the property with the right of survivorship. The right of survivorship means that a joint tenant's interest disappears upon his/her death and the remaining joint tenants' interests automatically expand to absorb it. As a result, although a joint tenant can sever the joint tenancy by conveying his/her interest to another during life (thereby creating a tenancy in common), a joint tenant cannot devise his/her interest at death.

Here, the husband and wife were joint tenants with the right of survivorship. Therefore, the husband could not sever the joint tenancy by devising his interest to his best friend. And since the husband and wife's joint tenancy remained intact, the wife absorbed his interest and became the sole owner of the land upon his death.

(Choice A) A tenant can unilaterally end a joint tenancy without the other tenant's consent. But this only occurs when a joint tenancy interest is conveyed during a tenant's lifetime, since a joint tenancy interest cannot be devised upon death.

(Choice B) Ademption is the failure of a gift under a will, often because the testator no longer owns that gift when he/she dies. Here, the best friend's interest in the land (not the wife's) adeemed because the husband's joint tenancy interest disappeared upon his death. Therefore, the husband had no interest to devise to his friend.

(Choice C) The doctrine of after-acquired title (ie, estoppel by deed) applies when a testator acquires title to devised property after executing a will. In that case, the property passes under the will so long as the testator still owns the property when he/she dies. This doctrine does not apply here since the husband (testator) owned the land before he attempted to devise it to the best friend.

📌 Educational Objective

A joint tenancy includes the right of survivorship, so a joint tenant's interest disappears upon his/her death and the remaining joint tenants' interests automatically expand to absorb it. As a result, a joint tenancy interest cannot be devised.

📚 References
  • 20 Am. Jur. 2d Cotenancy and Joint Ownership § 22 (2018) (severance of joint tenancy).
questions.zh-question:
一对夫妻以普通法上的共同共有（joint tenants with right of survivorship）的形式获得了一块土地。一年后，在妻子不知情的情况下，丈夫订立了一份遗嘱，将其在该土地上的权益遗赠给他最好的朋友。丈夫随后去世。

妻子现在是该土地的唯一所有权人吗？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为共同共有人有单方面的权利在未经其他共同共有人同意的情况下终止共同共有关系。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为妻子于丈夫未分割的50%土地所有权中所享有的权益已撤销（adeemed）。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为“事后取得产权”（after-acquired title）原则，或称“文书禁反言”（estoppel by deed）原则。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为对朋友的遗赠并未切断（sever）该共同共有关系。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Concurrent estates

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：联权共有（joint tenancy）里，遗嘱处分（devise）不能切断 生存者权（right of survivorship），所以死后那份会自动并入另一方。

三秒认题路径：

联权共有 → 写了遗嘱 → 不是生前转让 → 不会切断 → 配偶全得

核心法律规则

联权共有（joint tenancy）的考场意思：两个人各有一份未分割权益，但谁先死，谁那份就直接消失，由活着的人吸收。

生前转让（convey during life）可以切断联权共有；但死亡时遗嘱处分（devise at death）不行，因为人一死，自己已经没有可处分的产权了。

所以这里丈夫把份额写进遗嘱给朋友，并没有把联权共有切开；丈夫死后，妻子自动拿到全部土地。

核心判例： 本题逻辑与联权共有的一般规则一致：joint tenant 只有在生前转出权益时才可能切断联权共有，死亡时不能再用遗嘱处分自己的那份。

思维导图

先问：这是“死前转让”还是“死后遗嘱”？
题干事实丈夫只是执行遗嘱（executed a will），不是生前把份额转出去。
法律关卡
联权共有的切断点只看生前处分（inter vivos transfer）。
✘ 遗嘱处分不能切断联权共有
结果 丈夫死时他的份额已被生存者权（right of survivorship）吸收，妻子成为唯一所有人。
答案 选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然丈夫“写了遗嘱”，那他好像已经把自己的那一半送给朋友了。

但考试真正问的是：这是不是一种能切断联权共有的转让；答案是否，因为这只是死后处分（devise），不是生前切断。

这里看的是“活着的时候有没有把产权转走”，不是“死后遗嘱写没写”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干关键点是丈夫只是立遗嘱给朋友，没有生前转让，所以联权共有没被切断，妻子一死后自动吸收全部权益。

❌ 概念混淆 | 生前切断误判

✕ A: 把 unilaterally end 误当成死后也能做。

❌ 事实误判 | 份额消失误判

✕ B: 把对朋友的赠与说成adeemed，但妻子的份额根本没被消灭。

❌ 法律适用 | 事后取得误判

✕ C: 把 after-acquired title 套到已拥有的土地上，场景完全不对。

这题建议用什么方法？

先盯“生前转让还是死后遗嘱”，再看联权共有有没有被切断。

考场速记

记忆口诀：联权共有看生前，遗嘱处分不切断；人死份额自动并，生存者权直接收。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A man owned a tract of land in fee simple. By will duly admitted to probate after his death, the man devised the land to "any wife who survives me for life with remainder to such of my children as are living at her death."
The man was survived by his wife and by two daughters and a son. Thereafter, the son died and by will duly admitted to probate devised his entire estate to a friend. The son's sole heirs at law were the two daughters.
Later, the wife died. In an appropriate lawsuit to which the two daughters and the friend are parties, title to the land is at issue.
In such lawsuit, judgment should be that title to the land is in which party?

choices.A: The two daughters and the friend, because the earliest vesting of remainders is favored and reference to the wife's death should be construed as relating to time of taking possession.
choices.B: The two daughters and the friend, because the provision requiring survival of children violates the Rule Against Perpetuities since the surviving wife might have been a person unborn at the time of writing of the will.
choices.C: The two daughters, because the remainders were contingent upon surviving the life tenant.
choices.D: The two daughters, because the son's remainder must descend by intestacy and is not devisable.

questions.explanation:
Vested remainders v. Contingent remainders
Definition Examples
Vested Remainder not subject to condition precedent & held by identifiable living person
  • "... remainder to A"
Contingent Remainder subject to condition precedent or held by unknown / unborn person
  • "... remainder to A, but only if A outlives B"
  • "... remainder to my heirs"

A life estate终身地产权：在特定自然人（终身地产权人）生前享有占有不动产的现时权益，该权益在其死亡时终止。 is a present possessory interest in real property that expires upon the death of an individual. The future interest that follows a life estate is either a reversion (if it is held by the grantor) or a remainder (if it is created in a grantee — as seen here). A remainder is contingent if it is held by an unknown or unborn person OR subject to a condition precedent.

Here, the man devised a life estate in the land to his wife and a remainder to his children — but only if they survived the wife. Because the children's remainders were contingent upon surviving the wife, no child's interest can vest before the wife's death. This is true regardless of whether there is a policy favoring early vesting (Choice A). And since the son died before the wife, the son never acquired an interest in the land to devise to his friend. Therefore, the two daughters — both of whom were alive when the wife died — have title to the land.

(Choice B) A future interest that violates the Rule Against Perpetuities (RAP) is void. Therefore, had the children's remainders violated RAP, the daughters would not take title to the land.

(Choice D) Remainders (whether they are vested or contingent) are transferable inter vivos, devisable by will, and inheritable by intestate succession.

📌 Educational Objective

Future interests following a life estate are called remainders if they are created in a grantee. And remainders are contingent if they are

  • held by an unknown or unborn person or
  • subject to a condition precedent.
📚 References
  • Restatement of Property § 157 cmt. u (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (contingent remainders).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子以完全保有地产权(fee simple)的形式拥有一块土地。该男子去世后，其遗嘱经正式遗嘱认证程序确认，将该土地遗赠给“在我去世后尚存的妻子，为其终身保有，剩余权益则归于其去世时仍在世的我的子女。”

该男子去世时，其妻子、两个女儿和一个儿子尚在人世。此后，儿子去世，其遗嘱经正式遗嘱认证程序确认，将其全部遗产遗赠给了一位朋友。该儿子的法定继承人仅为其两个姐妹。

之后，妻子去世。在一场以两个女儿和那位朋友为当事人的相关诉讼中，该土地的所有权成为争议焦点。

在该诉讼中，应判决该土地的所有权归属于哪一方？

zh-choices.A: 两个女儿和那位朋友，因为法律倾向于剩余权益的尽早归属(vesting)，且提及妻子去世应被解释为与占有时间相关。
zh-choices.B: 两个女儿和那位朋友，因为要求子女生存的条款违反了反永久权规则(Rule Against Perpetuities)，因为存活的妻子在遗嘱订立时可能是一个尚未出生的人。
zh-choices.C: 两个女儿，因为剩余权益是以在终身地产权人(life tenant)之后存活为条件的或有权益(contingent)。
zh-choices.D: 两个女儿，因为儿子的剩余权益必须通过无遗嘱继承进行传承，且不可通过遗嘱处分。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Future interests

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：余留权益（remainder）到底是既得还是或有，以及“子女必须活到终身地产权人死亡”这个条件会不会让已死儿子的份额根本没活过来。

三秒认题路径：

先看终身地产权 → 再看余留权益 → 有生存条件 → 儿子先死 → 只剩两女儿

核心法律规则

这题只用到的规则

当未来权益由受让人取得时，叫余留权益（remainder）；如果它要等某个条件先成就，或者持有人在条件满足前还无法确定，就是或有余留权益（contingent remainder）。

这里的条件是“活到妻子死亡”，所以孩子们在妻子死前都不能确定拿到。考场意思：先死的儿子根本没有可继承、可遗赠的份额。

等妻子一死，活着的两个女儿才真正取得土地；这就是这题的终点，不是“尽量早既得”那套好听话。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用；本题真正锁定结论的是传统未来权益规则：有生存条件的余留权益在条件满足前不既得。

思维导图

先问：这是“终身地产权后面的余留权益”吗？
是 继续看持有人是谁：子女作为受让人取得，先定性为 remainder。
再问 这份权益要不要先满足“活到妻子死亡”？
要。这里的生存条件就是 condition precedent，所以在妻子死前不能既得。
结果 儿子先死时，还没拿到任何可转让份额 → 不能遗赠给朋友。
最后 妻子死时仍活着的两女儿满足条件 → 土地归两女儿。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：题目说“越早既得越好”，那儿子的份额应该先保护起来，再转给朋友。

但考试真正问的是：这个份额在妻子活着时有没有已经成立；答案是没有，因为“活到她死”本身就是门槛。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干把余留权益直接附上surviving the life tenant，所以这是或有余留权益；儿子先死，就没拿到任何份额，最后只有两女儿取得土地。

❌ 概念混淆 | 早既得误判

✕ A: 把“尽早既得”当成万能钥匙，硬读出不存在的提前确定。

❌ 法律适用 | RAP误套

✕ B: 盯着 Rule Against Perpetuities 乱打，题干根本没考无效，只考生存条件。

❌ 事实误判 | 先决条件漏读

✕ D: 以为儿子“已经有了”可遗赠份额，其实他在条件成就前就死了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先定性余留权益，再盯条件先决；只要“活到某人死亡”这句存在，就先别急着找既得。

考场速记

记住一句：“有条件先不既得；先死的人，份额还没到手。” 看到“survives / outlives”这类词，先问是不是条件先决，再决定谁能拿、谁不能遗赠。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A testator owned a tract of land in fee simple. The testator wrote and executed, with the required formalities, a will that devised the land to "my daughter for life with remainder to my descendants per stirpes." At the time of writing the will, the testator had a husband and no descendants living other than her two children, the daughter named in the will and a son.
The testator died and the will was duly admitted to probate. The testator's husband predeceased her, but she was survived by her daughter, her son, four grandchildren, and one great-grandchild. The testator's children were her sole heirs at law.
The testator's children brought an appropriate action for declaratory judgment as to title of the land. Guardians ad litem were appointed and all other steps were taken so that the judgment would bind all persons interested.
In that action, the court ruled that the daughter has a life estate in the whole of the land and that the remainder is contingent.
The court must have chosen a construction that did which of the following?

choices.A: Implied a condition that remaindermen survive the daughter.
choices.B: Implied a gift of a life estate to the son.
choices.C: Related all vesting to the death of the testator.
choices.D: Related all vesting to the time of writing of the will.

questions.explanation:
Vested remainders v. Contingent remainders
Definition Examples
Vested Remainder not subject to condition precedent & held by identifiable living person
  • "... remainder to A"
Contingent Remainder subject to condition precedent or held by unknown / unborn person
  • "... remainder to A, but only if A outlives B"
  • "... remainder to my heirs"

A remainder is a future interest in real property that is capable of becoming possessory upon the expiration of a life estate终身地产权：在特定自然人（终身地产权人）生前享有占有不动产的现时权益，该权益在其死亡时终止。 or term of years. Remainders are either:

  • vested — not subject to any condition precedent AND held by an identifiable living person or
  • contingent — subject to some condition precedent (other than the natural termination of the prior estate) OR held by an unknown or unborn person.

Here, the testator wrote a will that devised a life estate to her daughter and a remainder to her descendants. After the testator's death, the court ruled that the remainder was contingent — not vested. This means that the court cannot have chosen a construction (ie, interpretation) of the testator's will that related all vesting to:

  • the time of the writing of the will — in which case, the testator's descendants who were alive and identifiable when she wrote the will (her two children) would have had vested remainders (Choice D) or
  • the death of the testator — in which case, the testator's descendants who were alive and identifiable when she died (her children, grandchildren, and great-grandchild) would have had vested remainders (Choice C).

Instead, the court must have chosen a construction of the testator's will that implied a condition that remaindermen survive the daughter. In that case, the remainder would be contingent because the testator's descendants who will survive the daughter and eventually take possession of the land are still unknown.

(Choice B) There is no indication that the court implied a life estate to the son. And even if it did, this would not create a contingent remainder.

📌 Educational Objective

A vested remainder is not subject to any condition precedent and is held by an identifiable living person, whereas a contingent remainder is either subject to a condition precedent or held by an unknown or unborn person.

📚 References
  • Restatement of Property § 157 (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (discussing the types of remainders).
questions.zh-question:
一位立遗嘱人以无条件继承地产权（fee simple）的方式拥有一片土地。该立遗嘱人以法定形式书写并签署了一份遗嘱，将该土地遗赠给“我的女儿终身持有，剩余地产权由我的后嗣按房继承（per stirpes）”。

在书写遗嘱时，立遗嘱人有一位丈夫，除了她的两个孩子（遗嘱中指定的女儿和一个儿子）外，没有其他在世的后嗣。

立遗嘱人去世后，其遗嘱被正式接纳进行遗嘱认证（probate）。立遗嘱人的丈夫先于她去世，但她留下了女儿、儿子、四个孙子女和一个曾孙子女。立遗嘱人的子女是她的唯一法定继承人（heirs at law）。

立遗嘱人的子女就该土地的所有权提起了适当的宣告性判决（declaratory judgment）之诉。法院任命了诉讼监护人（Guardians ad litem），并采取了所有其他必要措施，以确保判决对所有利害关系人均具有约束力。

在该诉讼中，法院裁定女儿对全部土地拥有终身地产权（life estate），且剩余地产权（remainder）是或有的（contingent）。

法院必定是采纳了以下哪一种解释？

zh-choices.A: 默示了一个条件，即剩余地产权人（remaindermen）必须在女儿之后仍然在世。
zh-choices.B: 默示了将终身地产权（life estate）赠与儿子。
zh-choices.C: 将所有权利的归属（vesting）与立遗嘱人的死亡相关联。
zh-choices.D: 将所有权利的归属（vesting）与遗嘱的书写时间相关联。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Present estates

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：遗嘱里写“给女儿终身地产，再给后代”时，法院是不是把“后代必须活到女儿之后才能拿”这个条件读进去了，从而把余留权益判成 或有余留权益（contingent remainder）。

三秒认题路径：

终身地产 → 余留权益 → 看是否附条件 → 要求存活女儿 → 或有余留

核心法律规则

余留权益（remainder）是前一地产结束后才会开始占有的未来权益。若该权益 不附先决条件（not subject to condition precedent），并且由一个可识别的在世人持有，就是 已归属余留权益（vested remainder）；反过来，只要法院读出一个 先决条件（condition precedent），或者受益人还没确定、甚至可能尚未出生，就是 或有余留权益（contingent remainder）。 本题里，法院既然说“余留权益是或有的”，就等于它把“后代必须活过女儿”这个条件读进了遗嘱，所以现在还不知道最后谁能拿到地。

核心判例： Restatement of Property § 157 — 用“是否有先决条件、受益人是否已确定”锁定 vested v. contingent 的分界。

思维导图

先看：这是不是一个已经确定能拿的人？
不是： 只有“我的后代”这种集合描述，谁最后活到女儿之后还不确定。
再看：法院有没有加一个活到女儿之后的条件？
有： 一旦要求 remaindermen survive the daughter，就变成先决条件，余留权益不再 vested。
没有： 若只按写遗嘱时或死亡时去认定已确定受益人，就会落到已归属余留，和题干结论冲突。
结论怎么落？
答案： 法院必须是把“后代存活到女儿之后”当成条件，所以选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：题干里已经有女儿、儿子、孙辈和重孙辈，人数都很明确，好像应该直接算 vested remainder。

但考试真正问的是：法院有没有把“谁最后能活到女儿之后”当成门槛；只要有这个门槛，就不是现在立刻归属，而是等条件成就才知道谁拿。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干已把女儿设为 life estate，法院又说余留权益是或有的，说明它一定是要求后代活到女儿之后才拿，所以是加了生存条件。

❌ 概念混淆 | 误认受益人

✕ B: 把儿子硬塞成单独终身地产人，题干根本没给这种分割。

❌ 法律适用 | 死亡时点误判

✕ C: 若只看 testator death，题干这些后代早就都能固定下来。

❌ 事实误判 | 写作时点偷换

✕ D: 以写遗嘱当下定格，会把已在世子女直接变成 vested，和“or contingent”冲突。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“谁最后能拿”而不是“谁现在名字看起来最完整”，再看法院有没有偷偷加上存活条件。

考场速记

记住一句：可识别 + 无先决条件 = vested；要活到未来某时点或受益人未定 = contingent。看到“my descendants”这类词，先问“最后是不是还要活过前一地产人”，通常这就是题目想塞进去的条件。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A tenant entered into a one-year agreement to lease a two-bedroom home from a landlord for $1,000 per month, with rent due at the beginning of each month. The lease further provided that either party could properly terminate the lease by giving at least 30-days' notice. For eight months, the tenant paid rent on a timely basis. At the beginning of the following month, the tenant failed to pay rent. The landlord immediately contacted the tenant and demanded payment, but the tenant refused to pay. Pursuant to the terms of the lease, the tenant gave 30 days' notice of his intent to vacate the premises. The landlord subsequently sued the tenant for damages. In the meantime, the landlord re-rented the home for the remaining three months of the lease to another tenant for $800 per month.
Under the majority rule, what is the most that the landlord could potentially collect from the tenant?

choices.A: Nothing, because the landlord did not give the tenant the opportunity to cure before re-renting.
choices.B: $1,000, because the lease was properly terminated and the tenant is not obligated to pay future rents.
choices.C: $1,600, because the tenant is liable for any deficiency resulting from his early termination of the lease.
choices.D: $2,000, because the tenant is liable for the current month and rent that accrues during his 30-day notice period.

questions.explanation:
Landlord's remedies for tenant's failure to pay rent
Sue for rent
  • Can sue for rent as it comes due, several accrued rents, or entire amount at end of lease term
  • Majority rule – cannot recover future rents unless lease contains acceleration clause
  • Minority rule – can recover future rents minus (1) reasonable rental value of premises for remainder of lease or (2) actual rent collected on re-rental
Terminate & evict
  • Majority rule – must give tenant notice & opportunity to cure before terminating lease or evicting tenant
  • Minority (common law) rule – cannot evict tenant for failure to pay rent

A tenant has a duty to pay rent when it comes due. When a tenant fails to pay rent, the landlord may either sue for rent or terminate the lease and evict the tenant (see table).

When a tenant breaches a lease by failing to pay rent, the landlord may be entitled to damages. But under the majority rule, the doctrine of anticipatory repudiation does not apply to leases. Therefore, the landlord is not entitled to damages for future rents unless the lease contains a rent-acceleration clause.

Here, the tenant failed to pay rent at the beginning of the ninth month and then gave 30 days' notice of his intent to vacate the premises. The landlord re-rented the home for the remaining three months of the lease to another tenant for $800 per month.

Therefore, under the majority rule, the most the landlord could potentially collect from the tenant in this scenario is the one month's rent that the tenant failed to pay—ie, $1,000.

*Some leases contain rent-acceleration clauses, which allow the landlord to recover the entire unpaid rent for the remainder of the lease term upon the tenant's breach. But there is no indication that this lease contains such a clause.

(Choice A) The requirement that a landlord give notice and an opportunity to cure applies when the landlord seeks to terminate the lease and evict the tenant for failure to pay rent. Here, the tenant sought to terminate the lease by giving 30 days' notice. Therefore, the landlord was not required to give the tenant an opportunity to cure before re-renting the premises.

(Choices C & D) Under the minority rule, the doctrine of anticipatory repudiation applies to leases. This means that when a tenant breaches a lease, the landlord can sue for future rents, minus either:

  • the reasonable rental value of the premises for that period or
  • the actual rent collected on a re-renting of the premises for that period.

Under this rule, the landlord could potentially recover $1,600—ie, $4,000 in future rents ($1,000 × 4 months) minus $2,400 in actual rent collected on re-rental ($800 × 3 months). But the question asks what the landlord could collect under the majority rule.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the majority rule, the doctrine of anticipatory repudiation does not apply to leases. Therefore, a landlord generally cannot recover damages for future rents unless the lease contains a rent-acceleration clause.

📚 References
  • 49 Am. Jur. 2d Landlord and Tenant § 615 (2020) (time to sue in actions for recovery of rent).

主题：不动产法（Real Property）— 不动产所有权（Ownership of Real Property）

题目：
一名承租人（tenant）与房东（landlord）签订了一份为期一年的租赁协议，以每月1,000美元的租金租下了一栋两卧室住宅，租金应于每月月初支付。该租约还规定，任何一方只要提前至少30天通知，即可适当终止租约。前8个月，承租人都按时支付了租金。在随后一个月的月初，承租人未支付租金。房东立即联系承租人并要求付款，但承租人拒绝支付。根据租约条款，承租人发出30天通知，表示其将搬离该房屋。此后，房东起诉承租人要求赔偿损失。与此同时，房东将该房屋在租约剩余的3个月期间再次出租给另一名承租人，每月租金800美元。

根据多数规则（majority rule），房东最多可能向承租人收取多少？

zh-choices.A: 无，因为房东在重新出租前没有给承租人补救（cure）的机会。
zh-choices.B: 1,000美元，因为租约已被适当终止，承租人没有义务支付未来租金。
zh-choices.C: 1,600美元，因为承租人应对其提前终止租约所导致的任何差额（deficiency）负责。
zh-choices.D: 2,000美元，因为承租人应对当月租金以及其30天通知期间内产生的租金负责。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Landlord-tenant law

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：房客欠租后，房东在多数规则下只能追讨已经到期的租金，不能把剩余租期的未来租金一并算进去。

三秒认题路径：

欠租 → 终止/续租 → 看多数规则 → 未来租金不追 → 只算已到期

核心法律规则

租客的支付租金义务（duty to pay rent）到期就要付。若租客不付，房东可以选择追租（sue for rent），但在多数规则下，预期违约（anticipatory repudiation）一般不适用于租约，所以房东通常不能直接拿未来整段租期的租金当损失。

这道题里，房东真正能抓住的只有那一个月已经到期但没付的 $1,000；后面再租出去拿到的租金，不会把“未来租金”自动变成可全额追偿的项目。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用本题；本题锁定的是租约里多数规则不把未来租金当成可立即追讨的损失。

思维导图

先问：房东现在能不能把“整段剩余租期”都算进损害？
NO租约下的多数规则：预期违约（anticipatory repudiation）通常不适用。
卡死点：不能把未来租金直接当成可追偿损失。
YES只看已经到期且没付的租金；本题就是 第九个月房租 $1,000。
Trap“已经重新出租”不等于“可以把剩余三个月全算进去”——那是少数规则或有加速条款时才会想到的路。
Answer房东最多收回 $1,000。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：房东都已经把房子再租出去了，那就该把剩余租期的损失一起算出来。

但考试真正问的是：多数规则下，租约里未来租金能不能直接追，不是房东后来有没有重新找到租客。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干只显示一个月租金到期未付，且多数规则不让房东把后续 future rents 一并追成损失，所以最多就是 $1,000。

❌ 概念混淆 | 终止程序误判

✕ A: 把 opportunity to cure 套到房东这边了；这题是租客自己先通知退租。

❌ 法律适用 | 少数规则误判

✕ C: 这是把少数州的未来租金差额规则硬搬来。

❌ 事实误判 | 30天通知偷换

✕ D: 把 notice period 也算成额外欠租了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是不是多数规则下的租约追租题，再只抓已经到期的租金，不要被后续续租事实带跑。

考场速记

记住一句：租约欠租先算已到期租金（rent as it comes due），多数规则下未来租金（future rents）不能直接全追；看到“重新出租”先别激动，先问有没有加速条款（acceleration clause）。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A real estate developer owned a 100-acre tract of land. Six years ago, the real estate developer leased a one-acre lot located in the northeasterly corner of the tract for a term of 30 years to a fast-food company. The fast-food company intended to, and did, construct a fast-food restaurant on the one-acre lot.
The lease provided that:
The fast-food company was to maintain the lot and improvements thereon, to maintain full insurance coverage on the lot, and to pay all taxes assessed against the lot.
The real estate developer was to maintain the access roads and the parking lot areas platted on those portions of the tract that adjoined the lot and to permit the company's customers to use them in common with the customers of the other commercial users of the remainder of the tract.
The fast-food company was to pay its share of the expenses for the off-site improvements according to a stated formula.
Five years ago, the real estate developer sold the one-acre lot to an investor; the conveyance was made subject to the lease to the fast-food company. However, the investor did not assume the obligations of the lease and the real estate developer retained the remainder of the 100-acre tract of land. Since that conveyance five years ago, the fast-food company has paid rent to the investor. However, the fast-food company refused to pay its formula share of the off-site improvement costs as provided in the lease.
The real estate developer brought an appropriate action against the fast-food company to recover such costs.
Is the real estate developer likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the conveyance of the one-acre lot to the investor terminated the privity of estate between the real estate developer and the fast-food company.
choices.B: No, because the investor, as the fast-food company's landlord, has the obligation to pay the maintenance costs by necessary implication.
choices.C: Yes, because the conveyance of the one-acre lot to the investor did not terminate the real estate developer's right to enforce the covenant to contribute.
choices.D: Yes, because the use of the improvements by the customers of the fast-food company imposes an implied obligation on the fast-food company.

questions.explanation:
Assignee-landlord's right to enforce lease covenant that runs with land

Did the original parties to lease intend to bind assignee-landlord?
Yes
↓
No →
Original landlord can enforce
Does the covenant affect land's use or value (ie, touch & concern)?
Yes
↓
No →
Original landlord can enforce
Do the tenant and the assignee-landlord have a mutual or successive relationship (ie, privity of estate)?
Yes
↓
New owner can enforce
No →
Original landlord can enforce

A landlord may generally transfer his/her property interest to a third party (ie, assignee-landlord) without the tenant's consent. However, the assignee-landlord only has the right to enforce a covenant (ie, promise) in the lease if it runs with the land. Otherwise, the original landlord retains the right to enforce it. A covenant runs with the land when:

  • the original parties intended to bind successors in interest (eg, assignee-landlord)
  • the covenant touches and concerns (ie, affects the use or value of) the land and
  • the transfer brings the assignee-landlord into privity of estate (ie, a mutual or successive relationship in the same property interest) with the tenant.

Here, a lease covenant required that the fast-food company contribute to costs associated with off-site improvements on the real estate developer's adjoining property. This covenant did not touch and concern the one-acre lot because it only affected the adjoining property. Therefore, the covenant does not run with the land, and the conveyance to the investor did not terminate the developer's right to enforce that covenant.

(Choice A) Privity of estate between the real estate developer (landlord) and the fast-food company (tenant) terminated when the one-acre lot was sold to the investor. But the developer retains the right to enforce the covenant to contribute because the covenant does not run with the land.

(Choice B) The implied warranty of habitability obligates landlords to pay maintenance costs to keep property fit for residential purposes. But this obligation does not apply to commercial leases (as seen here). Even if it did, this would not affect the real estate developer's recovery of off-site improvement costs.

(Choice D) An implied obligation to contribute to repair and maintenance costs arises under an easement. But the use of the off-site improvements by the fast-food company's customers (easement) did not obligate the company to contribute to improvement costs.

📌 Educational Objective

A lease covenant can only be enforced by an assignee-landlord if it runs with the land. This occurs when (1) the original parties intended to bind their successors, (2) the covenant touches and concerns the land, and (3) there is privity of estate.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Prop.: Landlord & Tenant § 16.2 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (landlord's right to enforce lease provision against former tenant after transfer of ownership).
questions.zh-question:
一位房地产开发商拥有一块100英亩的土地。六年前，该房地产开发商将这块土地东北角的一块一英亩地块出租给一家快餐公司，租期为30年。该快餐公司计划并确实在该一英亩地块上建造了一家快餐店。

租赁合同规定：

1. 快餐公司须维护该地块及其上的改良物，为该地块维持全面的保险，并支付针对该地块征收的所有税款。

2. 房地产开发商须维护与该地块相邻的土地部分上规划的通行道路和停车场区域，并允许快餐公司顾客与该土地剩余部分的其他商业用户的顾客共同使用这些设施。

3. 快餐公司须根据既定公式支付其在场外改良物费用中的份额。

五年前，房地产开发商将这一英亩地块出售给一位投资者；此次转让受与快餐公司租赁合同的约束。然而，该投资者并未承担租赁合同中的义务，且房地产开发商保留了100英亩土地的剩余部分。自五年前那次转让以来，快餐公司一直向该投资者支付租金。然而，快餐公司拒绝按照租赁合同的规定，支付其按公式计算的场外改良物费用份额。

房地产开发商对快餐公司提起了适当的诉讼，以追讨该等费用。

房地产开发商可能胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为将一英亩地块转让给投资者终止了房地产开发商与快餐公司之间的财产利益关系（privity of estate）。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为作为快餐公司的出租人，投资者有因必要默示而支付维护费用的义务。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为将一英亩地块转让给投资者并未终止房地产开发商执行该缴款契约的权利。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为快餐公司的顾客对改良物的使用为快餐公司施加了一项默示义务。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Assignment and subletting

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：原出租人把土地转给买受人后，租约中的约定（lease covenant）到底还能不能由原出租人继续主张，关键看这个约定有没有随地负担（run with the land）。

三秒认题路径：

租约转让 → 约定能否随地 → 原房东还有无权利 → 看触地牵连 → 选能继续起诉的一边

核心法律规则

租约里的契约（covenant），只有在原始当事人本意是约束继受人、该约定touch and concern土地、并且新旧当事人之间存在privity of estate（物权性关系）时，才会随地而走。考场意思：这时新房东才能去告；否则，还是原房东有权主张。

这里的关键是：被要求分担的是“邻地”上的off-site improvements费用，它没有真正改变这块一英亩租地本身的使用或价值，所以通常不 touch and concern这块租赁地。考场意思：不随地，就不因卖地给投资人而把原出租人的起诉权一起卖掉。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Property: Landlord & Tenant § 16.2 — 传给买受人后，若约定不随地，原房东仍可向前承租人追讨。

思维导图

原房东把一英亩地卖给投资人后，自己还能不能继续追 fast-food company 的分担费用？
先看：这个约定有没有随地负担（run with the land）？
第1关：原始租约有没有想绑定继受人？
第2关：约定有没有触地牵连（touch and concern）？
这里被卡死：只管邻地 off-site improvements，不是这块租地本身的使用或价值。
第3关：是否存在物权性关系（privity of estate）？
结论：不随地 → 原房东保留起诉权 → 选 C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：土地已经卖给投资人了，privity of estate 断了，所以原房东也不能再管了。

但考试真正问的是：这个约定到底会不会run with the land。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这里的损失点不是“谁现在是房东”，而是“这个费用义务本来就没随地走”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干off-site improvements只影响邻地，不触及这块租地本身，所以该分担义务不随地转移，原房东仍可追讨。

❌ 概念混淆 | 关系断裂误判

✕ A: 把 privity of estate 断掉当成一刀切，忽略原房东仍可主张不随地的约定。

❌ 法律适用 | 住宅规则误搬

✕ B: 乱搬 habitability 到商用租约，还想借此替房东免除该费用。

❌ 事实误判 | easement 偷换

✕ D: 把客户使用通道硬说成 implied obligation，题干并没给出这种维修分担义务。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定“约定会不会随地”，再看触地牵连；一旦不随地，原房东通常还能追。

考场速记

记住一句：租约约定要随地，先看 intent，再看 touch and concern，最后看 privity of estate；只要卡在触地牵连，原房东往往还能继续起诉。

这类题别被“房子已经卖了”带跑，先问：义务到底是不是跟着地走。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
An owner of land devised the land to a specific university "for the purpose of conducting field research for the improvement of agricultural products and for no other purpose." The owner devised all of her other real property interests to her granddaughter. The owner's only heir was her son. Later, the university decided to build a science classroom on the land even though using the land for the enumerated purpose was still practicable. The owner's granddaughter, asserting ownership of the land, sought to evict the university from the land.
There is no applicable statute, and the common law Rule Against Perpetuities is unmodified in the jurisdiction.
If the court rules in favor of the university, what is the most likely reason?

choices.A: The cy pres doctrine applies to the university's current use of the land.
choices.B: The granddaughter's executory interest in the land is void under the Rule Against Perpetuities.
choices.C: The owner's son, not the granddaughter, is the proper plaintiff to seek eviction.
choices.D: The university owns the land in fee simple absolute because the devise did not include conditional or durational language.

questions.explanation:
Fee simple estates
Type Language Future interest
Indefeasible
Fee simple absolute
  • “To A”
  • “To A and his heirs”
 None
Defeasible, Durational
Fee simple determinable
  • “so long as”
  • “during”
  • “until”
 Grantor’s possibility of reverter
Third party’s executory interest (ie, fee simple subject to executory limitation)
Defeasible, Conditional
Fee simple subject to condition subsequent
  • “but if”
  • “provided that”
  • “unless”
 Grantor’s right of entry

Like a fee simple absolute (FSA), a defeasible fee is ownership of potentially infinite duration. But unlike an FSA, a defeasible fee can be terminated by the occurrence of a stated event. Defeasible fees are limited by specific durational or conditional language (eg, “so long as,” “but if”). However, language that limits only the purpose of the transfer (eg, “for the purpose of”) creates an FSA.

Here, the owner’s devise did not include conditional or durational language. Instead, the owner devised the land to the university “for the purpose of conducting field research for the improvement of agricultural products and for no other purpose.” This conveyance created an FSA — not a defeasible fee — so the university is free to do with the land as it sees fit (eg, build a science classroom thereon). For that reason, the court will most likely rule in favor of the university.

(Choice A) The cy pres doctrine allows courts to reform the conveyance of a future interest — not the university’s present interest — to come as close as possible to the transferor’s intent while preventing it from violating the Rule Against Perpetuities.† Additionally, this doctrine only applies to a charitable gift or trust when the charitable objective is or later becomes impossible or impracticable to fulfill (not seen here).

(Choices B & C) The owner’s conveyance created an FSA, which has no associated executory interest or other future interest. As a result, neither the son nor the granddaughter has an interest in the land. But had the owner conveyed a defeasible fee and retained the associated future interest, the granddaughter (not the son) would hold that future interest. That is because the owner left all of her other real property interests to the granddaughter.

†The Rule Against Perpetuities (RAP) does not apply to future interests held by the grantor. Therefore, had the granddaughter succeeded to a future interest held by the owner (eg, possibility of reverter), it would not be subject to RAP.

📌 Educational Objective

Defeasible fees are limited by specific durational or conditional language (eg, “so long as,” “but if”). Language that limits only the purpose of the transfer creates a fee simple absolute.

📚 References
  • Restatement of Property § 44 cmt. m (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (discussing designated purpose of conveyance).
questions.zh-question:
一位土地所有者将土地遗赠给一所特定大学，‘用于进行旨在改良农产品的田野研究，且不得用于任何其他目的。’该所有者将其所有其他不动产权益遗赠给了她的孙女。该所有者唯一的继承人是她的儿子。后来，尽管将土地用于上述列明目的仍然可行，该大学仍决定在该土地上建造一间科学教室。该所有者的孙女主张对该土地的所有权，并试图将该大学从土地上驱逐出去。

该司法管辖区内没有适用的成文法，且普通法中的Rule Against Perpetuities（反永久所有权规则）未经修改。

如果法院作出有利于该大学的裁决，最可能的原因是什么？

zh-choices.A: cy pres原则适用于该大学目前对土地的使用。
zh-choices.B: 根据Rule Against Perpetuities，孙女在该土地上的待执行权益是无效的。
zh-choices.C: 该所有者的儿子，而非孙女，才是寻求驱逐的适格原告。
zh-choices.D: 该大学拥有该土地的完全永久所有权（fee simple absolute），因为遗赠中不包含条件性或期限性语言。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Present estates

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：目的性措辞（for the purpose of） 只是写明用途，不等于给了 可撤销简单费（defeasible fee）。

三秒认题路径：

只写用途 → 无条件词 → 不是可撤销 → 变成FSA → 选D

核心法律规则

简单产权绝对（fee simple absolute） 是最完整的现今产权，考场意思：除非题干写了明确的限制词，否则受让人可以按自己想法使用土地。可撤销简单费（defeasible fee） 只有在题干出现 so long as、until、but if、unless 这类语言时才会成立。单写 “for the purpose of” 只是在讲用途，考场意思：它不会自动变成条件或期限。

核心判例： Restatement of Property § 44 cmt. m 的思路是：指定用途不等于附条件，所以上述措辞通常仍给出 fee simple absolute。

思维导图

先看题干有没有真正的限制词？
没有 这里只有 “for the purpose of conducting field research”，没有 so long as / but if / unless。
卡死点：只写用途，不写终止条件 → 不是 defeasible fee
结果 受让人拿到的是 fee simple absolute，所以现在能改建科学教室。
顺手排除
别被 cy pres 牵走：那是修复公益性未来利益，不是改写现在的所有权。
答案 D：不是可撤销简单费，而是 FSA

考点陷阱

你可能会想：题目说了“只能用于研究”，那学校一改用途就该输。

但考试真正问的是：这句话有没有写成真正的限制条件；这里只有用途描述，没有条件词，所以不能把它硬拗成 defeasible fee。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干只有 for the purpose of，没有条件或期限词，所以学校拿到的是 fee simple absolute，当然可以继续按自己需要使用土地。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把公益目的直接当成 cy pres，但这不是在改未来利益。

❌ 法律适用 | 未来利益误套

✕ B: 题干根本没给出可撤销简单费，哪来的执行性未来利益和 RAP 问题。

❌ 事实误判 | 继承人身份偷换

✕ C: 先假设有人能拿回地再谈原告资格，但这里学校本来就不是违约占地。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓措辞：看到的是用途限制还是条件限制，别被“目的”两个字带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：用途词不等于条件词；看到 for the purpose of 先问自己“有没有 so long as / but if / unless”，没有就优先判 fee simple absolute。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
An entrepreneur owned a ranch. He entered into a written three-year lease of the ranch with a rancher. Among other provisions, the lease prohibited the rancher from "assigning this lease, in whole or in part, and from subletting the ranch, in whole or in part." In addition to a house, a barn, and a one-car garage, the ranch's 30 acres included several fields where first the entrepreneur, and now the rancher, grazed sheep.
During the following months, by a written agreement, the rancher allowed his neighbor, a car enthusiast, exclusive use of the garage for storage, under lock and key, of his antique automobile for two years, charging him $240. The rancher told his other neighbor, a golfer, that she could use the fields to practice golf as long as she did not disturb his sheep.
Which, if any, of the rancher's actions constituted a violation of the lease?

choices.A: Only allowing the car enthusiast exclusive use of the garage for storage.
choices.B: Only allowing the golfer to use the fields to practice her golf.
choices.C: Both actions.
choices.D: Neither action.

Licensee can use property

Unless the lease expressly provides otherwise, a tenant is free to transfer his/her interest under the lease to a third party through either:

  • assignment – a transfer of all, or part of, the tenant's interest under the lease to a third party for the remainder of the tenant's lease term or
  • subletting – a transfer of all, or part of, the tenant's interest under the lease to a third party for less than the remainder of the tenant's lease term.

Here, the entrepreneur leased his ranch to the rancher for three years. The lease expressly prohibited the rancher from assigning or subletting the ranch, in whole or in part. The rancher then entered into a written agreement that gave the car enthusiast exclusive possession of the ranch's garage (part of the rancher's lease interest) for two years (less than the remainder of the rancher's lease term) in exchange for $240. Therefore, this written agreement was a sublease and violated the entrepreneur and rancher's lease (Choices B & D).

A tenant also is generally free to grant a license – a non-possessory (and usually non-exclusive) right to enter and use the property for a particular purpose – to a third party unless the lease states otherwise. Here, the lease only prohibited assigning and subletting. Therefore, the rancher's license to the golfer – granting her a non-exclusive right to enter and use the property to practice golf – did not violate the lease (Choices B & C).

📌 Educational Objective

A tenant generally has the right to (1) transfer his/her interest under a lease for the remainder (assignment) or part (sublease) of the lease term or (2) grant a non-possessory right to use the property for a particular purpose to another (license). However, these rights can be restricted by an express lease provision.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Prop.: Landlord & Tenant §§ 15.1–15.2 (1977).
  • Restatement of Prop. § 512 (1944).
questions.zh-question:
一名企业家拥有一处牧场。他与一名牧场主就该牧场签订了一份为期三年的书面租赁合同。除其他条款外，该租赁合同禁止牧场主“全部或部分转让本租约（assigning this lease），以及全部或部分分租（subletting）该牧场”。该牧场占地30英亩，除了一栋房屋、一个谷仓和一个单车位车库外，还包括几片此前由企业家本人、现由牧场主用来放羊的田地。

在接下来的几个月里，牧场主通过一份书面协议，允许他的邻居（一位汽车爱好者）在两年内独家使用车库，并上锁存放其古董车，为此向邻居收取240美元。牧场主告诉他的另一位邻居（一位高尔夫球手），只要不打扰他的羊，她就可以使用那些田地练习高尔夫。

牧场主的哪些行为（如有）构成了对租赁合同的违反？

zh-choices.A: 仅允许汽车爱好者独家使用车库进行存放的行为。
zh-choices.B: 仅允许高尔夫球手使用田地练习高尔夫的行为。
zh-choices.C: 两种行为均构成。
zh-choices.D: 两种行为均不构成。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Assignment and subletting

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：看租客把权利给别人时，是转让（assignment）、转租（sublease），还是只是许可（license），以及哪一种会违反 lease 里的禁止条款。

三秒认题路径：

先看条款禁不禁 → 再看是否占有 → 再看期限长短 → 再分 assignment / sublease / license → 再判是否违约

核心法律规则

一般规则是：除非 lease 另有规定，承租人可以把自己在 lease 下的利益转给第三人。把全部或部分租赁利益给出去，且第三人取得的是剩余租期中的权利，这叫转让（assignment），考场意思：把“剩下的租期”整段或一部分交出去。

如果第三人拿到的是少于剩余租期的时间，就是转租（sublease），考场意思：你把手里的一段时间再切出去。若只是给别人一个非占有性的使用权，就是许可（license），考场意思：能用，但不拿占有权。

核心判例：本题对应的标准就是普通法下的 lease transfer 规则：exclusive possession 加上期限切分，通常会把“看起来像授权”变成 sublease；而非独占、非占有的使用通常只是 license。

思维导图

先问：这是不是把租赁利益交给第三人？
A.给了 独占占有（exclusive possession） + 只给两年，少于剩余租期
卡死点：这不是单纯许可，而是 转租（sublease）；又因为 lease 明文禁止 sublet，所以 违约。
B.只允许非独占使用，且只是练球，没拿占有
这条走 许可（license），不等于 transfer of possession，所以 不违约。
结论题干里只有车库那笔会触发禁止条款，答案落在 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：车库只给了两年，好像只是“借用”一下，不算太大动作。

但考试真正问的是：有没有把 exclusive possession 给出去；有的话，法律会优先把它当成 sublease 来看。

司法考试看的是「权利结构有没有变」，不是「故事听起来像不像临时借用」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干里车库是 exclusive use，而且给了两年，属于把部分租赁利益切出去的 sublease；lease 又明文禁转租，所以这一笔违约。

❌ 概念混淆 | 使用当占有

✕ B: 把 use the fields 看成占有，其实只是许可。

❌ 法律适用 | 双项全错

✕ C: 车库那笔才触发禁令，不是两笔都错。

❌ 事实误判 | 独占事实漏读

✕ D: 漏看车库是 exclusive use，所以不能说都没违约。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“独占占有 + 剩余期限”这两个信号，再把非独占使用直接排成 license。

考场速记

记住一句：占有看 assignment / sublease，单纯使用看 license。先问对方有没有拿到 possession，再问期限是不是少于剩余租期。

口诀可以记成：“独占+分期=转租；只用不占=许可。”

question_analysis.skill_tested: Distinguish subleases from non-possessory licenses

keywords.text: assigning this lease, in whole or in part

reason.en: Expressly restricts transferring any part of the tenant's leasehold interest.
reason.zh: 明确限制承租人转让其租赁权益的任何部分。

keywords.text: subletting the ranch, in whole or in part

reason.en: Bars transferring possession for less than the remaining lease term.
reason.zh: 禁止在剩余租期未满时向他人转移占有。

reason.en: Exclusive possession of part of the premises signals a sublease, not a license.
reason.zh: 对部分物业的独占使用表明是转租而非许可。

reason.en: A two-year grant is less than the three-year lease remainder, supporting sublease classification.
reason.zh: 两年期限短于三年租约剩余期，支持认定为转租。

reason.en: Payment for exclusive use reinforces a transfer of possessory interest.
reason.zh: 为独占使用付费强化了占有权益的转移。

keywords.text: use the fields to practice golf

reason.en: A purpose-limited, non-exclusive use is characteristic of a license.
reason.zh: 限定用途且非独占的使用符合许可特征。

keywords.text: as long as she did not disturb his sheep

reason.en: Shows the rancher retained possession and control, indicating a license.
reason.zh: 表明承租人仍保留占有与控制，说明是许可而非转租。

reason.en: Correctly identifies the only arrangement that transferred exclusive possession.
reason.zh: 正确指出唯一构成转移独占占有的安排。

B.text: use the fields to practice her golf

reason.en: Tempts test-takers to treat non-possessory permission as a prohibited sublease.
reason.zh: 诱使考生将非占有性许可误当作禁止的转租。

reason.en: Assumes any third-party use violates the lease, ignoring the license exception.
reason.zh: 假定任何第三方使用均违约，忽视许可例外。

reason.en: Treats the garage arrangement as a mere license despite exclusive possession and rent.
reason.zh: 尽管存在独占占有和租金，仍将车库安排视为普通许可。

highlights.text: the lease prohibited the rancher from "assigning this lease, in whole or in part, and from subletting the ranch, in whole or in part."

reason.en: Defines which tenant transfers are forbidden but does not bar licenses.
reason.zh: 界定禁止的承租人转让行为，但不禁止许可。

highlights.text: the rancher allowed his neighbor, a car enthusiast, exclusive use of the garage for storage, under lock and key, of his antique automobile for two years, charging him $240.

reason.en: Exclusive possession of part of the premises for less than the lease term constitutes a prohibited sublease.
reason.zh: 在短于租期的期限内对部分物业的独占占有构成被禁止的转租。

highlights.text: The rancher told his other neighbor, a golfer, that she could use the fields to practice golf as long as she did not disturb his sheep.

reason.en: Non-exclusive, revocable permission without transfer of possession is a license, not a sublease.
reason.zh: 非独占、可撤销且未转移占有的许可属于许可使用，而非转租。

highlights.text: by a written agreement

reason.en: A written grant of exclusive use supports classification as a sublease rather than a casual license.
reason.zh: 书面授予独占使用支持认定为转租而非随意许可。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A widow created a testamentary trust to which she devised real property that was rented under a long-term lease. The trust was to pay the income from the trust to the widow's son for life and then accumulate the income from the trust until the son's first-born child reached 30 years of age, at which time the trust property was to be distributed to that child. Neither the will nor the trust contained any specific provision for distribution of the trust property if the son's first-born child were to die before reaching the age of 30. At the time of the widow's death, the widow's son had no children. Subsequently, the son had a child.
The son has recently died. His only child is now five years old. The trustee has sought a judicial ruling as to what to do with the trust property.
The applicable jurisdiction continues to follow the common law Rule Against Perpetuities but modifies it in accord with the cy pres doctrine.
If the court determines that the trust violates the Rule Against Perpetuities, what should the court order the trustee to do?

choices.A: Maintain the trust under its existing terms, because the cy pres doctrine allows the trust to continue under its existing terms despite violating the Rule Against Perpetuities.
choices.B: Maintain the trust until the child either lives for another 21 years or dies, because the cy pres doctrine allows the trust to be reformed as close as possible to the grantor's intent.
choices.C: Terminate the trust, because the child's interest in the trust violates the Rule Against Perpetuities and cannot be saved under the cy pres doctrine.
choices.D: Terminate the trust, because the child's interest in the trust violates the Rule Against Perpetuities and the cy pres doctrine applies only to charitable gifts.

questions.explanation:
Rule Against Perpetuities (RAP)

Renders contingent future interests void if they could vest more than 21 years after some life in being when interest was created:

Traditional common law rule
  • Contingent remainders
  • Executory interests
  • Vested remainders subject to open
  • Powers of appointment
  • Rights of first refusal
  • Options
Reforms
  • "Wait & see" stance (most jurisdictions) – otherwise invalid interest is valid if it vests within 90 years of its creation
  • Cy pres doctrine (few jurisdictions) – otherwise invalid interest will be reformed to come "as close as possible" to grantor's intent without violating RAP

The Rule Against Perpetuities (RAP) applies to contingent future interests in grantees, where the grantee is unascertained or there is a condition precedent to the interest becoming vested. RAP renders these interests void if they could vest more than 21 years after the end of some life in being when the interest was created. Here, the child's future interest in the trust is subject to RAP because it is contingent upon the child's reaching 30 years of age. And it violates RAP because the 5-year-old child cannot turn 30 within 21 years of the son's death.

However, this jurisdiction applies the cy pres doctrine to interests that violate RAP. This doctrine allows a court to make changes to a conveyance to come "as close as possible" to the grantor's actual intent without violating RAP (Choice C). Here, the widow did not provide for an alternative taker in the event that the child's interest failed, so her intent was to save the child's interest in the trust if possible. Therefore, the court should change the age contingency and order the trustee to maintain the trust until the child lives for another 21 years (or dies).

(Choice A) The cy pres doctrine allows courts to reform a conveyance to prevent it from violating RAP; it does not allow a trust that violated RAP to continue under its existing terms.

(Choice D) While the cy pres doctrine is most often applied by courts to save a gift to charity, it can also be applied when RAP would void a contingent future interest in a noncharitable grantee (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

In a few jurisdictions, the cy pres doctrine allows a court to reform a conveyance to come as close as possible to the grantor's intent while staying within the bounds of the Rule Against Perpetuities – eg, by reducing the time limit for a future interest to vest to 21 years after the end of the last life in being when the interest was created.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Property: Donative Transfers § 1.5 (Am. Law Inst. 1983) (applying cy pres principles to reform interests that would otherwise fail under the Rule Against Perpetuities).
questions.zh-question: 一位寡妇设立了一项遗嘱信托，她将一处根据长期租赁合同出租的不动产遗赠给该信托。该信托将在寡妇儿子在世期间向其支付信托收入，然后累积信托收入，直到其儿子的长子女年满30岁，届时将信托财产分配给该子女。遗嘱和信托中均未包含任何具体条款，以规定在其儿子的长子女年满30岁前去世的情况下，该如何分配信托财产。在寡妇去世时，她的儿子没有子女。后来，该儿子有了一个孩子。 最近，儿子去世了。他唯一的孩子现在五岁。受托人已请求法院就如何处理信托财产作出裁决。 适用的司法管辖区继续遵循普通法上的 Rule Against Perpetuities，但根据 cy pres 原则对其进行修改。 法院应如何裁决？

zh-choices.A: 命令受托人维持该信托，直到该子女再活21年或去世为止，因为法院可以根据 cy pres 原则修改该财产转让。
zh-choices.B: 命令受托人维持该信托，直到该子女年满30岁或去世为止，因为 cy pres 原则允许信托按其现有条款继续存在。
zh-choices.C: 命令受托人终止该信托，因为该子女在信托中的权益违反了 Rule Against Perpetuities，且无法被补救。
zh-choices.D: 命令受托人终止该信托，因为 cy pres 原则仅适用于慈善赠与。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Future interests

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：当未来受益权违反 永续规则（Rule Against Perpetuities, RAP） 时，这个州是否用 cy pres doctrine 把信托改写到尽量接近立遗嘱人的意思，而不是直接照原条款硬撑到底。

三秒认题路径：

未来受益权 → RAP 失效 → 有 cy pres → 改期限救回 → 不是直接维持原样

核心法律规则

考场上只抓这几句

RAP（Rule Against Perpetuities）专打 contingent future interests：只要它有可能在“某个在世生命结束后再过 21 年”之外才 vest，就会失效。这里孩子必须满 30 岁才拿到财产，所以对一个 5 岁孩子来说，明显可能超过 21 年，先撞上 RAP。

但这题所在法域还认 cy pres doctrine，考场意思：法院不让原条款原封不动地活着，而是把年龄条件改到 as close as possible 的位置，尽量保住立遗嘱人的安排。

所以这题不是“信托照旧继续”，而是“把 30 岁改成不违反 RAP 的期限”，让 trustee 先继续持有，直到孩子再活 21 年或死亡。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Property: Donative Transfers § 1.5 的思路就是：用 cy pres 去改写本来会被 RAP 打掉的处分，使其尽量接近赠与人的真实意思。

思维导图

先问：这是 终局判给（final judgment） 吗？
否再看有没有法定中间上诉；没有就进 附带命令原则（collateral-order doctrine）。
三要件是否都过？
1. 独立于实体争议？
2. 重要到足以先处理？
3. 终局后仍可有效复审（effectively reviewable）？
卡死点：第 3 项没过。
披露命令即使难受，终局后仍能撤销、发回、重审，仍可救。
看到 律师-当事人特权（attorney-client privilege） 的 强制披露令（motion to compel / order to compel production），联想 Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter。
结论：通常 不能立刻上诉，要等终局判决后再说。
答案
B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：特权资料一旦泄露就“回不去了”，所以应该马上上诉。

但考试真正问的是：不是看你怕不怕泄密，而是看终局后还能不能通过上诉把错误救回来。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

所以别被“害得很惨”带跑；collateral-order doctrine 的关键是第 3 项，能不能 effectively reviewable。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干里孩子要到 30 岁才拿到信托利益，而孩子现在才 5 岁，先撞上 RAP；本州又允许 cy pres doctrine，所以法院应把期限改到尽量接近原意的 21 年范围内继续维持信托。

❌ 概念混淆 | 原样维持误判

✕ A: 把 cy pres 误当成“原条款照旧继续”。

❌ 法律适用 | 直接作废误判

✕ C: 只看到 RAP 失效就想一刀切作废，漏掉了本州会改写救回。

❌ 事实误判 | 慈善限定误判

✕ D: 把 charitable gifts 想成唯一适用场景，题干明明是非慈善受益人。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓 RAP 是否被触发，再看本州有没有 cy pres 去“改期限救回”。

考场速记

记忆口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，先记“有法定例外才可提前上诉”，再记 injunction、certification、class action 这些常见入口。

做题时一句话：看到特权披露令，先想 Mohawk，再问“终局后还能不能救”。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Reform invalid future interest under cy pres

reason.en: Determines whether the child's future interest is void for remoteness.
reason.zh: 决定子女未来权益是否因过远而无效。

reason.en: Authorizes judicial reformation instead of automatic invalidation.
reason.zh: 授权法院改革信托条款而非直接宣告无效。

reason.en: Sets the conveyance structure and measuring lives for RAP.
reason.zh: 确立财产转移结构及禁止永久权规则的衡量生命。

reason.en: Creates a contingent future interest that may vest too remotely.
reason.zh: 创设可能过远归属的条件性未来权益。

reason.en: Shows the child cannot satisfy the age-30 condition within 21 years after the son's death.
reason.zh: 表明儿子死后21年内子女无法满30岁。

reason.en: Triggers the trustee's request and starts the relevant RAP measuring period.
reason.zh: 触发受托人申请并启动相关禁止永久权衡量期。

reason.en: The asset whose administration the court must order after RAP analysis.
reason.zh: 经禁止永久权分析后法院须决定如何管理的资产。

reason.en: Misstates cy pres as permitting an unreformed, RAP-violating trust.
reason.zh: 误称就近原则允许违反禁止永久权规则的信托原样存续。

A.text: despite violating the Rule Against Perpetuities

reason.en: Suggests cy pres excuses the violation rather than reforms it.
reason.zh: 暗示就近原则可豁免违反而非通过改革补救。

B.text: lives for another 21 years or dies

reason.en: Matches the reformed vesting period that saves the grantor's intent within RAP.
reason.zh: 符合在禁止永久权范围内挽救设立人意图的改革归属期。

B.text: reformed as close as possible to the grantor's intent

reason.en: States the correct judicial remedy when RAP voids the original contingency.
reason.zh: 说明原条件因禁止永久权无效时法院应采的正确救济。

C.text: cannot be saved under the cy pres doctrine

reason.en: Denies reformation even though this jurisdiction applies cy pres to RAP failures.
reason.zh: 否认可改革，但本辖区对禁止永久权失败适用就近原则。

reason.en: Wrong remedy when cy pres can reform rather than destroy the disposition.
reason.zh: 在就近原则可改革时错误的救济方式。

reason.en: Overstates a common charitable use as the sole scope of cy pres here.
reason.zh: 将慈善场景的常见适用误当作本案唯一范围。

reason.en: Follows from the false premise that cy pres cannot save this interest.
reason.zh: 源于就近原则不能挽救该权益的错误前提。

highlights.text: modifies it in accord with the cy pres doctrine

reason.en: Signals that invalid interests should be reformed, not simply voided or left unchanged.
reason.zh: 表明无效权益应被改革，而非简单作废或维持原状。

highlights.text: until the son's first-born child reached 30 years of age

reason.en: The contingent condition that creates the RAP problem.
reason.zh: 创设禁止永久权问题的条件性归属。

highlights.text: His only child is now five years old

reason.en: Proves vesting at 30 cannot occur within 21 years after the son's death.
reason.zh: 证明儿子死后21年内无法满30岁归属。

highlights.text: If the court determines that the trust violates the Rule Against Perpetuities, what should the court order the trustee to do?

label.zh: 违反禁止永久权后的命令

reason.en: Asks for the court's remedial order once cy pres applies to a failed contingency.
reason.zh: 要求在条件失败且适用就近原则时法院应下达的命令。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
Seven years ago, a man, his sister, and his cousin became equal owners, as tenants in common, of a house. Until a year ago, the man lived in the house alone. The sister and the cousin are longtime residents of another state.
One year ago, the man moved to an apartment and rented the house to a tenant for three years under a lease that the man and the tenant both signed. The tenant has since paid the rent each month to the man.
Recently, the sister and the cousin learned about the rental. They brought an appropriate action against the tenant to have the lease declared void and to have the tenant evicted. The tenant raised all available defenses.
What will the court likely decide?

choices.A: The lease is valid, and the tenant is not evicted but must share possession with the sister and the cousin.
choices.B: The lease is valid, and the tenant retains exclusive occupancy rights for the balance of the term.
choices.C: The lease is valid, but the tenant is evicted because one-third of the lease term has expired and the man had only a one-third interest to transfer.
choices.D: The lease is void, and the tenant is evicted.

questions.explanation:
Consent between cotenants in common
(common examples)
Consent required No consent required
Convey entire co-owned property Sell, lease, or devise personal ownership interest
Obtain exclusive possession over part of property Possess entire co-owned property
Bind other cotenants' interests in contract with third party Extract minerals from co-owned property (unless committing waste)

Tenancy in common is concurrent ownership of property where each co-tenant has a separate share of the property but the right to possess and enjoy the entire property (ie, separate but undivided interests). A tenant in common may lease or otherwise transfer his/her property interest to a third party without the other co-tenants' consent. But the other co-tenants are entitled to:

  • possess and use the entire property with the third party and
  • share expenses and income (eg, rent) generated by the property in proportion to their property interests.

Here, the man, sister, and cousin share the house as tenants in common. The man leased the house to a tenant, who then paid rent to the man. And though the sister and cousin only recently learned of this lease, it is valid (not void) because the man did not need their consent to lease his property interest. As a result, the court will likely decide that the tenant is not evicted but must share possession with the sister and cousin (Choices B & D).

(Choice C) Although the man (an equal owner) had only a one-third interest in the house, he was entitled to lease his right to possess and enjoy the entire house to the tenant. And since two-thirds of the lease term still remain, the tenant should not be evicted.

📌 Educational Objective

A tenant in common has the right to lease (or otherwise transfer) his/her separate, undivided property interest to a third party without the other co-tenants' consent. But the other co-tenants have the right to share possession of the property with the third party and receive a share of the rental income in proportion to their property interests.

📚 References
  • 20 Am. Jur. 2d Cotenancy and Joint Ownership § 31 (2018) (defining tenancy in common).

zh-choices.B: 租赁合同有效，租户在剩余租期内保留独家占用权。
zh-choices.C: 租赁合同有效，但租户被驱逐，因为三分之一的租期已过，而该男子仅有三分之一的权益可供转让。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Concurrent estates

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：共有产权（tenancy in common）里，一个共有人能不能把自己那份租给第三人，答案是能，但不能赶走其他共有人。

三秒认题路径：

共有人 → 租给第三人 → 不用同意 → 不能排他占有 → 只能共用

核心法律规则

这题只要抓住一条

共有产权（tenancy in common）下，每个共有人都有各自独立、但未分割的份额，所以可以把自己的份额卖掉、租出去，或者设立遗嘱处分。租赁（lease）第三人后，第三人只是接手该共有人能让出的占有权，不能把其他共有人赶出去。

所以考试上要先问：租约是不是当然无效？不是。更准确的结果是：租约有效，但其他共有人仍有权进入并共同占有，租金也按份额分配。

核心判例： 20 Am. Jur. 2d Cotenancy and Joint Ownership § 31：共有人可处分自己的份额，但不能单方面绑定其他共有人。

思维导图

男方共有人 只转让自己的份额
→
受租人 拿到占有权，但不是唯一占有人
→
其他共有人 无需同意，但可共同占有并分租金
先看：男方能不能租？
YES因为tenancy in common允许处分自己的separate, undivided interest。
再看：能不能把姐妹和表亲赶走？
NO其他共有人没有同意，不代表租约无效；失败点在“不能排除他们占有”
最后落点
结论租约有效，租客不能独占，只能和其他共有人共同占有，对应正确答案。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然姐妹和表亲没签字，lease void 吧。

但考试真正问的是：一个共有人能不能单独把自己的份额租出去，以及租客能不能排除其他共有人。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题的坑不是“没通知”，而是“把不能单独绑定别人误读成自己那份也不能转”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的tenants in common意味着男方可把自己的占有权租给第三人，租约有效；但姐妹和表亲仍可进入并共同占有，不能被赶走。

❌ 法律适用 | 排他占有误判

✕ B: 把exclusive occupancy当成共有人当然能给的。

❌ 概念混淆 | 份额期限误判

✕ C: 把男方只剩one-third当成只能租三分之一。

❌ 事实误判 | 同意要件偷换

✕ D: 见到没征求同意就以为void。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认共有形式，再问“能不能转自己的份额”，最后分清“有效转让”和“不能排除他人”两步。

考场速记

记住一句：tenancy in common 能租自己那份，不能独占整套房；能转让，不等于能赶人。遇到共有人出租题，先默念：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 不是这题的口诀，这题的口诀是“自己能租，别人能进”。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
An aunt owned a commercial property consisting of a one-story building rented to various retail stores and a large parking lot. Two years ago, the aunt died and left the property to her nephew for life, with remainder to her godson, his heirs and assigns. The devise of the property was made subject to any mortgage on the property in effect at the time of the aunt's death.
A year before her death, the aunt mortgaged the property to secure a loan of $150,000. The entire principal of the mortgage remained outstanding when she died. As a result, the net annual income from the property was reduced not only by real estate taxes and regular maintenance costs, but also by the substantial mortgage interest payments due each month.
A commercial real estate developer recently proposed to purchase the property and pay off the mortgage in order to demolish the existing building and construct a 30-story office building. The nephew was willing to accept the developer's offer. However, the godson refused the offer even though he, as the remainderman, paid the principal portion of each monthly mortgage payment. The godson wanted to convert the property into a public park when he became entitled to possession.
When the developer realized that the godson would not change his mind, it modified its proposal to a purchase of the nephew's life estate. When the godson learned that the nephew had agreed to the developer's modified proposal, the godson brought an appropriate action against them to enjoin their carrying it out.
What is the godson's best argument?

choices.A: Continued existence of the one-story building is more in harmony with the ultimate use as a park than the proposed change in use.
choices.B: The developer cannot purchase the nephew's life estate, because life estates are not assignable.
choices.C: The godson's payment of the mortgage principal has subrogated him to the nephew's rights as a life tenant and bars the nephew's assignment of the life estate without the godson's consent.
choices.D: The proposed demolition of the building constitutes waste.

questions.explanation:
Life tenant's duties
Duty to pay current charges Life tenant must pay all current charges due during life tenancy (eg, property taxes, mortgage interest) up to financial benefit received from property
Duty to prevent waste Life tenant must prevent affirmative waste (ie, voluntary waste), permissive waste & ameliorative waste
Duty to make ordinary repairs Life tenant must make reasonable repairs to preserve property

A life estate is a present possessory interest that terminates on the death of an individual. This interest is freely transferable (Choice B). But since it is followed by a future interest that will become possessory once the life estate terminates, the life tenant has a duty to prevent waste. There are three types of waste:

  • Affirmative waste – changes that decrease the property's value
  • Permissive waste – deterioration caused by neglect or the failure to reasonably protect the property
  • Ameliorative waste – changes that increase the property's value but are not necessary to make reasonable use of the property amid substantial and permanent changes in the local area

The future interest holder (the godson) may inspect the land for waste and may seek damages or an injunction to prevent waste. This ensures that the life tenant (the nephew) delivers the property to the future interest holder in essentially the same condition it was in when the life tenant took possession.

Here, the demolition of the building would change the condition of the property. Although the construction of a 30-story office building would likely increase the property value, there is no indication that this change is necessary. Therefore, the godson's best argument is that the proposed demolition constitutes waste.

(Choice A) A life tenant can use the property in any manner that does not constitute waste – even if that use affects the future interest holder's plans. Therefore, the godson's plan to use the property as a park is irrelevant.

(Choice C) The future interest holder is responsible for the mortgage principal, but this does not bar the life tenant from assigning the life estate or allow the future interest holder to subrogate the life tenant's rights. Instead, subrogation allows a third party who fully pays off a senior mortgage with no knowledge of junior interests to take that senior mortgage's priority.

📌 Educational Objective

A life tenant has a duty to prevent waste so that the property can be delivered in essentially the same condition it was in when the life tenant took possession.

📚 References
  • Restatement (First) of Property § 140 (Am. Law Inst. 1936) (life tenant's duty to prevent waste).
questions.zh-question:
一位姑母拥有一处商业地产，该地产包含一栋出租给多家零售商店的单层建筑和一个大型停车场。两年前，姑母去世，将该地产遗赠给她的侄子终身持有(for life)，剩余权益(remainder)则归于她的教子及其继承人和受让人。该地产的遗赠受制于姑母去世时该地产上存在的任何抵押权。

在姑母去世前一年，她将该地产抵押，以担保一笔15万美元的贷款。她去世时，该抵押贷款的全部本金仍未偿还。因此，该地产的年净收入不仅因房地产税和常规维护成本而减少，还因每月需支付的大量抵押贷款利息而减少。

最近，一位商业房地产开发商提议购买该地产并清偿抵押贷款，以便拆除现有建筑，建造一栋30层的办公楼。侄子愿意接受开发商的要约(offer)。然而，教子拒绝了该要约，尽管他作为剩余权益人(remainderman)，支付了每月抵押贷款偿还中的本金部分。教子希望在他有权占有该地产时，将其改造成一个公园。

当开发商意识到教子不会改变主意时，便将其提议修改为购买侄子的终身地产权(life estate)。当教子得知侄子已同意开发商修改后的提议时，教子对他们提起了适当的诉讼，以禁止他们执行该计划。

教子最好的论点是什么？

zh-choices.A: 保留单层建筑比提议的用途变更更符合其作为公园的最终用途。
zh-choices.B: 开发商不能购买侄子的终身地产权(life estate)，因为终身地产权不可转让。
zh-choices.C: 教子支付抵押贷款本金的行为使他代位取得了侄子作为终身地产权人(life tenant)的权利，并禁止侄子在未经教子同意的情况下转让其终身地产权。
zh-choices.D: 提议的拆除建筑行为构成了“耗损”(waste)。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Present estates

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：终身地产（life estate）能不能为了盖新楼被拆掉，关键看这是不是对未来权益人的浪费（waste）。

三秒认题路径：

life tenant → 想拆楼 → 伤及余留权益 → 先看 waste → 选 D

核心法律规则

拿分规则

终身地产（life estate）是当前占有性权益，但它后面跟着未来权益，所以终身承租人（life tenant）不能把财产弄得让未来权益人接手时明显变样。考试里只要看到拆楼、毁坏、永久改变使用方式，就先问这是不是积极浪费（affirmative waste）或改善性浪费（ameliorative waste）。

浪费（waste）的考场意思：不是看眼前值不值钱，而是看现在的动作会不会把房子从“原样交回”变成“被你改坏了”。

核心判例： Restatement (First) of Property § 140 — 终身承租人有义务防止浪费，保证把财产基本按接手时的状态交给未来权益人。

思维导图

先看：nephew 作为 life tenant，能不能同意开发商把楼拆掉？
关键事实一层商业楼 + 大停车场 + 提议拆成 30 层办公楼。
规则关卡只要是永久拆除、改造、改变不动产现状，就先往 affirmative waste / ameliorative waste 走。
拆楼是否必要、只是更赚钱，还是为了合理使用土地？
本题卡死点题干只说“可能升值”，没说这是必要改造。
没有必要性 → 不能拿“升值”洗掉 waste。
结论是什么？
答案godson 最强论点就是：proposed demolition constitutes waste，所以可申请禁令。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：开发商盖 30 层楼后房产价值更高，说明 godson 反对只是“挡发展”。

但考试真正问的是：life tenant 有没有权把未来权益人的标的物永久改掉；这里争的是waste，不是谁的商业计划更漂亮。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的 拆除一层楼并改建 30 层办公楼 会永久改变标的物现状，life tenant 不能靠“会升值”躲过 waste。

❌ 概念混淆 | 终局用途误判

✕ A: 把未来想做公园当成决定标准，但争点是现在能不能毁掉现有建筑。

❌ 法律适用 | 可转让性错套

✕ B: 误把 not assignable 套到 life estate；终身地产本来就能转让。

❌ 事实误判 | 代位关系偷换

✕ C: 把付贷款本金说成能锁死转让权，但 subrogated 不是这里的规则。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓占有人是否在改坏标的，再问这种改坏会不会伤到未来权益人。

考场速记

记住一句：life tenant 能用，不能毁；能赚钱，不能把房子改到后手接不住。看到“拆楼、改建、永久变化”，先秒连到 waste。

In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 这题不用；本题只背“未来权益人有权拦住浪费”就够了。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A landlord and a tenant entered into a valid written agreement to lease a single-family residence for a period of one year at $1,200 per month. Among the provisions in the agreement was a waiver of the implied warranty of habitability. Two months into the lease, the electricity stopped working through no fault of the tenant. The tenant notified the landlord, but after one week, the landlord had done nothing to remedy the problem. When the next month's rent came due, the tenant refused to pay it because the landlord had still not fixed the electricity. The landlord has filed an action for breach of contract against the tenant for failure to pay rent.
Who is likely to prevail?

choices.A: The landlord, because the tenant waived the implied warranty of habitability in the lease.
choices.B: The landlord, because there is no duty to repair under a residential lease.
choices.C: The tenant, because the landlord's failure to repair the electricity violated the implied covenant of quiet enjoyment.
choices.D: The tenant, because the tenant notified the landlord of the problem and gave him a reasonable opportunity to correct it.

questions.explanation:
Landlord's duty to repair leased premises
Type of lease Common law Majority rule
Residential No duty to repair unless statute or contract requires Duty to repair substantial defects under implied warranty of habitability
Commercial No duty to make ordinary repairs unless statute or contract requires

In most jurisdictions, landlords of leased residential properties have a duty to repair substantial defects that are not caused by the tenant. Failure to make such repairs violates the implied warranty of habitability, which ensures that residential properties satisfy basic safety and living conditions. If the warranty is violated, the tenant may:

  • refuse to pay rent until the necessary repairs are made
  • remedy the defect and offset those costs against the rent or
  • treat the condition as a constructive eviction*.

However, the tenant must notify the landlord of the problem AND give the landlord a reasonable opportunity to correct it before exercising these remedies.

Here, the electricity in the leased residence stopped working two months into the lease through no fault of the tenant. The tenant notified the landlord of this defect and gave him one week, a reasonable opportunity, to correct the problem. The landlord did nothing. Therefore, the tenant was entitled to withhold rent and is likely to prevail in this breach-of-contract action.

*Note that when claiming a breach of the warranty of habitability, the tenant is not required to vacate the premises unless the tenant chooses to treat the defect as a constructive eviction.

(Choice A) The implied warranty of habitability cannot be waived by a tenant, either by express language in the lease or by taking possession of the property with knowledge of the conditions.

(Choice B) At common law, a landlord had no implied duty to make repairs under a residential lease. However, landlords do have an implied duty to repair in most jurisdictions today.

(Choice C) The implied covenant of quiet enjoyment is a promise by the landlord not to interfere with the tenant's possession of the leased premises. Here, the landlord did not violate this covenant since the failure to repair the electricity did not interfere with the tenant's right to possess the leased residence.

📌 Educational Objective

In most jurisdictions, a residential landlord must repair substantial defects not caused by the tenant. Breach of this duty violates the implied warranty of habitability and allows the tenant to withhold rent if the landlord had a reasonable opportunity to correct the defect after notice.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Property: Landlord & Tenant § 5.5 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (landlord's duty to repair).

哪一方可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 房东，因为租户在租赁合同中放弃了默示可居住性保证。
zh-choices.B: 房东，因为住宅租赁合同中没有维修义务。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Duties Of Landlord

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：住宅租赁中，房东是否因未修好重大缺陷而违反适居性默示保证（implied warranty of habitability），从而让租客可以停付房租。

三秒认题路径：

住宅租约 → 停电缺陷 → 已通知房东 → 给过一周 → 可拒付租金

核心法律规则

在大多数州，住宅房东对不是租客造成的重大缺陷负有修理义务；如果房东不修，就会违反适居性默示保证（implied warranty of habitability），考场意思：房客不用继续按原样交租。

但租客要先通知房东（notice），还要给房东一个合理的修复机会；题干里已经给了一个星期，足够支撑租客先停付租金。

waiver 在这里救不了房东，因为这类保证通常不能被租客预先放弃。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Property: Landlord & Tenant § 5.5 — 住宅房东要修重大缺陷；通知后仍不修，租客可以拒付租金。

思维导图

1. 住宅租赁
题干是 single-family residence，先进入适居性默示保证（implied warranty of habitability）路线。
2. 重大缺陷
electricity stopped working，这不是小瑕疵，是会影响基本居住条件的缺陷。
3. 非租客所致
停电不是租客造成，所以房东不能把修理责任甩回去。
4. 已通知
租客已经告诉房东，满足notice 这一步。
5. 合理机会
给了 one week，考试里足以算合理修理机会。
6. 房东没修
卡死点：房东沉默不修，所以租客可以停付租金。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：题目写了 waiver，那房东就稳赢。

但考试真正问的是：住宅房东是否仍要修重大缺陷；这里真正能决定答案的是“已通知 + 已给合理修复机会”，不是那条放弃条款。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的 停电 属重大缺陷，租客已通知并给了房东一周修理机会，所以可以拒付房租并抗辩违约。

❌ 概念混淆 | 保证误放弃

✕ A: 把 waiver 当成万能挡箭牌，忽略这类保证通常不能预先放弃。

❌ 法律适用 | 旧法搬错场景

✕ B: 只背住普通法旧规则，没看到现代大多数州已经改成要修重大缺陷。

❌ 事实误判 | 侵扰对象偷换

✕ C: 把停电硬说成 quiet enjoyment 受侵扰，但这里没到干扰占有的程度。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是不是住宅，再看缺陷是否重大、是否已通知并给过合理修复机会。

考场速记

记住这句：住宅房东遇到重大缺陷，先看 适居性默示保证（implied warranty of habitability）；通知 + 合理机会 到位后还不修，租客就能停付租金。
