questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A dairy farmer and his cousin owned a large farm in fee simple as tenants in common, each owning an undivided one-half interest. For five years, the farmer occupied the farm and conducted farming operations. The farmer never accounted to his cousin for any income but did pay all real estate taxes when they were due and kept the buildings on the farm insured against loss from fire, storm, and flood. The cousin lived in a distant city and was interested only in realizing a profit from the sale of the land when market conditions produced the price he wanted.
The farmer died intestate survived by his daughter, who was his sole heir. Thereafter, the daughter occupied the farm but was inexperienced in farming operations. The result was a financial disaster. The daughter failed to pay real estate taxes for two years. The appropriate governmental authority held a tax sale to recover the taxes due. At the sale, the cousin was the only bidder and obtained a conveyance from the appropriate governmental authority upon payment of an amount sufficient to discharge the amounts due for taxes, plus interest and penalties, and the costs of holding the tax sale. The amount paid was one-third of the reasonable market value of the farm.
Thereafter, the cousin instituted an appropriate action against the daughter to quiet title in and recover possession of the farm. The daughter asserted all defenses available to her.
Except for the statutes related to real estate taxes and tax sales, there is no applicable statute.
In this lawsuit, is the cousin entitled to a decree quieting title so that he is the sole owner in fee simple of the farm?

choices.A: No, if the daughter pays the cousin one-half of the amount he paid for the tax deed.
choices.B: No, if the daughter pays the cousin one-half of the reasonable market value of the farm.
choices.C: Yes, because the cousin survived the farmer.
choices.D: Yes, because the daughter defaulted in the obligations undertaken by the farmer.

questions.explanation:
Farmer dies;
daughter inherits Taxes not paid Tax sale;
cousin buys Daughter fails
to contribute
Farmer Daughter
Cousin

A tenant who buys back co-owned property at a tax sale or foreclosure sale takes the property subject to the other co-tenants' interests. The nonpaying co-tenants then have a reasonable time to contribute their share of the purchase price (as determined by their proportionate ownership interests). A co-tenant who fails to do so forfeits his/her interest in the property to the purchasing co-tenant.

Here, the dairy farmer and his cousin each owned a one-half interest in the farm as tenants in common. When the farmer died, his daughter acquired his one-half interest in the farm. She failed to pay real estate taxes for two years, and a tax sale was held. At that sale, the cousin bought back the farm. But he will only be the sole owner of the farm if the daughter fails to contribute her one-half share of the purchase price.

(Choice B) The daughter need only pay the cousin half of the amount he paid at the tax sale to retain her one-half interest in the farm. The farm's reasonable market value is irrelevant.

(Choice C) The fact that the cousin survived the farmer would have entitled him to sole ownership of the farm had they been joint tenants. That is because a joint tenant's interest disappears upon death and the remaining tenants' interests automatically expand to absorb it (ie, right of survivorship). But tenants in common have no such right.

(Choice D) The daughter's default on tax obligations did not terminate her interest in the farm. Instead, her interest in the farm (or forfeiture thereof) depends on whether she pays the cousin her due contribution—half of the purchase price.

📌 Educational Objective

A tenant who buys back co-owned property at a tax or foreclosure sale takes the property subject to the other co-tenants' interests. But the other co-tenants must contribute their proportionate share of the purchase price within a reasonable time to avoid forfeiting their interests to the purchasing co-tenant.
questions.zh-question:
一位奶农和他的堂兄作为分权共有人（tenants in common），以完全所有权（fee simple）共同拥有一座大农场，每人拥有不可分割的二分之一权益。五年来，该奶农占有并经营该农场。奶农从未向其堂兄报告过任何收入，但按时支付了所有到期的房产税，并为农场上的建筑物投保了火灾、风暴和洪水险。堂兄住在一个遥远的城市，他唯一的兴趣是在市场行情达到他期望的价格时，通过出售土地来实现盈利。

奶农未立遗嘱而去世，其唯一继承人是他的女儿。此后，女儿占有该农场，但由于缺乏农场经营经验，导致了财务上的灾难。女儿连续两年未支付房产税。相关政府机构为收回欠税举行了一次税务拍卖。在拍卖会上，堂兄是唯一的竞标人，并在支付了足以清偿所欠税款、利息、罚金以及举行税务拍卖费用的金额后，从相关政府机构处获得了产权转让文书。他支付的金额是该农场合理市价的三分之一。

此后，堂兄对女儿提起了适当的诉讼，请求确认其对农场的所有权（quiet title）并收回占有。女儿提出了所有可用的抗辩。

除了与房产税和税务拍卖相关的法规外，没有其他适用的成文法。

在本案诉讼中，堂兄是否有权获得确认所有权的判决，从而成为该农场唯一的完全所有权人（owner in fee simple）？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，如果女儿向堂兄支付其为税务契据所付款项的一半。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，如果女儿向堂兄支付农场合理市价的一半。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为堂兄在奶农去世后仍然在世。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为女儿未履行奶农所承担的义务。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Concurrent estates

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：按份共有（tenants in common）里，一方在税收拍卖（tax sale）后买回共有房产，能不能直接把另一方的份额一刀切掉。

三秒认题路径：

按份共有 → 税拍买回 → 另一方没出钱 → 看能否补缴 → 不能直接独占

核心法律规则

如果共有人的一方在税收拍卖（tax sale）或止赎拍卖（foreclosure sale）中把共有房产买回，买回后仍要受其他共有人的份额约束。其他共有人只要在合理期间内补上自己按份额应出的价款，就能保住自己的利益；如果不补，才会把份额丢给买下房产的人。

这里的关键不是谁先死、谁最后买，而是另一方有没有按比例补钱。reasonable time 和 proportionate share 是考场关键词：先看份额，再看应付金额。

核心判例：本题对应的规则就是共有人在税拍中买回共有物后，仍须给其他共有人补缴情形下的赎回机会；所以不能因为对方没立刻出钱，就自动宣告买方拿到全部所有权。

思维导图

父亲与堂兄 按份共有，各 1/2
→
父亲死亡 女儿继受 1/2
→
女儿不缴税 触发 tax sale
→
堂兄买回 买回≠自动独占
→
女儿要补出 只补自己那一半
能不能直接 quiet title 变成唯一 fee simple？
先看：这不是 joint tenancy，所以没有 right of survivorship，不能靠“他比父亲活得久”拿全部。
再看：税拍买回后，女儿若在合理期间补上自己按份额应付的价款（proportionate share），就保住 1/2。
结论：她没补钱前，堂兄不能直接拿到全权；应先给她补缴情机会。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：堂兄是唯一买家，又付了税款和罚金，应该直接拿到整块地。

但考试真正问的是：另一共有人有没有机会按份额补钱，不是谁先掏了税款就谁自动赢。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的土地已经被谁买走」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

堂兄在tax sale买回的是共有财产，女儿只要补上自己一半购价（one-half of the amount），就能保住她的 1/2 份额。

❌ 事实误判 | 市价偷换

✕ B: 把补缴情金额偷换成 reasonable market value，题目根本看的是买价一半。

❌ 概念混淆 | 继承错位

✕ C: 把按份共有硬说成 survived 就能独占，混进了 joint tenancy 的规则。

❌ 法律适用 | 违约自动失权

✕ D: 以为女儿没缴税就自动丢份额，其实还要看她是否补出自己应付的那一半。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定共有类型，再盯住税拍买回后的补缴情规则，别被死亡和市场价带跑。

考场速记

记住这句：共有人买回共有物，其他共有人还能按份额补钱保份额；只有不补，才会把权利让出去。看见税拍、止赎拍卖、按份共有，就先问“who pays proportionate share”。

questions.subject: Real Property
questions.question:
A landowner granted a construction company the exclusive right to remove sand and gravel from the landowner's property for 20 years in exchange for a monthly payment of a fixed amount. The agreement was properly recorded. Three years later, the construction company purchased the landowner's property and built a plant for processing the sand and gravel on the property. Twelve years after purchasing the property, the construction company sold the portion of the land on which the sand and gravel was located to a buyer, while retaining the portion of the land on which the processing plant was located. The contract made no specific mention of the prior recorded agreement, but the construction company had come to rely on the supply of sand and gravel from the property. Although there are other sources for the sand and gravel, sand and gravel are necessary for the projects undertaken by the construction company. The buyer has refused to permit the construction company to continue to remove sand and gravel from the portion of the property purchased by the buyer.
Which of the following is the construction company's best argument for this profit?

choices.A: Sand and gravel are necessary for the construction company to operate.
choices.B: The buyer is estopped from denying the existence of the profit due to the construction company's reliance on the property as its source for sand and gravel.
choices.C: The profit exists by implication.
choices.D: The written agreement that created the profit was recorded.

questions.explanation:
Easements v. Profits
(methods of creation)
Express grant or reservationNecessityExisting prior usePrescriptionEstoppel
Easements
Profits

A profit is a nonpossessory right to enter another's land and remove specific natural resources-e.g., timber, sand, gravel. Similar to an easement, a profit can be implied from an existing prior use. This arises when the owner of two parcels of land used one parcel (servient parcel) to benefit the other (dominant parcel), and then one of those parcels was transferred to another. A profit will be implied if the prior use was (1) continuous, (2) apparent or known, and (3) reasonably necessary to the dominant parcel's use and enjoyment.

Here, the construction company owned two parcels-one that supplied (servient parcel) and another that processed (dominant parcel) sand and gravel. The company later sold the servient parcel to a buyer but made no mention of a profit. Nevertheless, the servient parcel's prior use (supplying sand/gravel) was likely continuous and apparent. And it was necessary for the dominant parcel's use and enjoyment because the company had come to rely upon that sand/gravel supply. Therefore, the company's best argument is that the profit exists by implication.

(Choice A) Although sand and gravel are necessary for the construction company's operations, profits cannot be created by necessity. And even if they could, no necessity exists here because other sources for sand and gravel are available.

(Choice B) A profit can be created by estoppel if there was good-faith, reasonable, and detrimental reliance on permission from the servient-parcel owner. But here, no such reliance occurred because the buyer refused to give the construction company permission to remove sand and gravel from the servient parcel.

(Choice D) Although the landowner granted the construction company an express profit that was in writing and recorded, that profit terminated by merger when the company acquired title to the dominant and servient parcels.

📌 Educational Objective

A profit by implication can stem from prior use when (1) the owner of a servient and dominant parcel of land transfers one of those parcels to another and (2) the prior use of the servient parcel was continuous, apparent or known, and reasonably necessary to the dominant parcel's use and enjoyment.
questions.zh-question:
土地所有人授予一家建筑公司在20年内有权从该土地所有人的土地上专有地移除沙子和砾石（sand and gravel），作为交换，该公司按月支付固定金额。该协议已依法妥善登记（recorded）。三年后，建筑公司购买了该土地所有人的土地，并在该地块上建造了一座用于加工沙子和砾石的工厂。购买该土地十二年后，建筑公司将沙子和砾石所在的那部分土地卖给了一名买方，而保留了建有加工工厂的那部分土地。该买卖合同并未具体提及此前已登记的协议，但建筑公司已经开始依赖该地块提供沙子和砾石。尽管还有其他沙子和砾石来源，但这些材料对建筑公司承接的项目是必要的。买方拒绝允许建筑公司继续从其购买的那部分土地上移除沙子和砾石。

以下哪一项是建筑公司主张该 profit 最好的论据？

zh-choices.A: 沙子和砾石对建筑公司开展经营是必要的。
zh-choices.B: 由于建筑公司一直依赖该土地作为沙子和砾石的来源，买方因 estoppel（禁止反言）而不得否认该 profit 的存在。
zh-choices.C: 该 profit 是通过 implication（默示）产生的。
zh-choices.D: 创设该 profit 的书面协议已经登记（recorded）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Real Property: Ownership of Real Property - Ownership of Real Property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：原先连续、可见且对现在使用有必要的土石采掘使用，在分割转让后能否被推定为默示利润（profit by implication）。

三秒认题路径：

采砂权 → 已记录 → 先共用 → 后分售 → 默示利润

核心法律规则

利润（profit）是进入他人土地并移除特定自然资源的非占有性权利（nonpossessory right），比如 sand、gravel、timber。考试里最常见的是看它能不能从既往使用（existing prior use）推出来：原来同一所有人把一块地拿来给另一块地提供资源，后来卖掉其中一块，就可能把这项权利“带”过去。

要成立默示利润（profit by implication），前提是先前使用要持续（continuous）、明显或已知（apparent or known），而且对受益地块的使用与享受合理必要（reasonably necessary）。这题里公司先同时持有供砂地和加工地，后来分开转让，所以最强理由不是“必要性”本身，而是既往使用被默示保留。

核心判例：本题对应的是 profit by implication from prior use 的标准：先有连续、明显、且对受益地块合理必要的既往使用，后有分割转让，利润就可能被默示保留下来。

思维导图

原始状态 同一土地所有人
→
供砂地 servient parcel
→
加工地 dominant parcel
→
分割出售 未提及利润
先看：这不是靠“必要”直接生出来的权利，而是靠“既往使用”默示保留吗？
1. 先前供砂是否连续、可见/已知？
是：供砂长期、现场可见，容易被默示保留。
2. 对加工地是否合理必要？
是：公司已经依赖这条供给线，离开它就不好运作。
3. 能不能改走“必要性”或“estoppel”？
不能：有别的来源不等于能直接做成必要；也没有买方诱导式许可。
结论：最强答案 = 默示利润存在 → 选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：砂石是工程要用的，所以只要“很需要”就能把利润做出来。

但考试真正问的是：这项权利是不是从既往使用（prior use）默示出来，而不是单靠“业务需要”硬推。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这题对应地也是看权利来源能不能成立，不是看公司主观上有多依赖。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干里原本同一所有人先把采砂地拿来供加工地使用，后来又分开转让，且该使用长期、明显并对加工地有现实依赖，所以最强论点是profit exists by implication。

❌ 事实误判 | 资源必要偷换

✕ A: 把“业务需要”当成独立来源，忽略了权利来源要靠既往使用。

❌ 概念混淆 | 许可依赖误认

✕ B: 这里没有买方诱导的许可依赖，estoppel 这条线走不通。

❌ 法律适用 | 合并灭失误套

✕ D: 录音本身不是现在的取胜点，先前权利已因合并而不再靠它单独撑住。

这题建议用什么方法？

先找权利来源，再看是否有连续、可见、且对受益地块合理必要的既往使用。

考场速记

记住一句：利润（profit）不是“我很需要”就自动有，而是看旧时的共享使用能不能被默示带到新所有关系里。

速记：prior use + continuous + apparent/known + reasonably necessary，四步齐了，才更像 profit by implication。
